motivation: To make real-time fermionic dynamics classically tractable by exploiting weak interactions, locality, and Anderson localization.
method: Combines continuous-time QMC, diagrammatic QMC, and Majorana Propagation with a new Heisenberg-picture operator-growth analysis to rigorously control sampling complexity.
result: Achieves polynomial-time algorithm for local observables when interaction strength is below a threshold independent of system size; extends to quasi-polynomial for Frobenius norm and to larger coupling with localization.
conclusion: Identifies broad parameter regimes where weak interactions and locality render classical simulation of fermionic dynamics efficient.

title: In-situ Time-domain Physical Adjoint Optimization Of Complex Wave Dynamics
authors: Hoyeong Kwon, Arunn Suntharalingam, Laureano Bulus-Rossini, Tsampikos Kottos
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Direct optimization of complex wave dynamics through the intrinsic evolution of physical systems is fundamentally limited by the lack of directly accessible gradients. Adjoint methods provide an exact route to gradient computation and have enabled optimization in numerical solvers and, more recently, in frequency-domain physical platforms. Yet their extension to the time domain has remained out of reach, as reproducing time-reversed propagation appears to require non-causal operations or compensating gain. Here we develop a protocol and experimentally demonstrate that time-domain adjoint dynamics can be realized in-situ in linear physical systems without gain, non-causal elements, or auxiliary backward networks. By combining time remapping with a transformation of system variables, we obtain a physically realizable adjoint evolution that constructs gradients from measurable signals. We experimentally demonstrate the approach in a complex RLC network, realizing in-situ optimization for time-dependent objectives, including time-windowed and broadband responses. This framework unifies physical optimization by enabling both system parameters and source excitations to be optimized within the same platform. Our results close the gap between adjoint theory and physical implementation, establishing a general foundation for hardware-native, in-situ temporal optimization across a broad class of complex dynamical systems.
tldr: This paper develops a protocol for in-situ time-domain adjoint optimization in physical systems without gain or non-causal elements, demonstrated in an RLC network.
motivation: Direct optimization in physical systems is limited by lack of accessible gradients, and time-domain adjoint methods have not been experimentally realized.
method: The authors combine time remapping with a transformation of system variables to construct physically realizable adjoint evolution, demonstrated experimentally in a complex RLC network.
result: They demonstrate in-situ optimization for time-dependent objectives, including time-windowed and broadband responses.
conclusion: This work establishes a general foundation for hardware-native, in-situ temporal optimization across complex dynamical systems.

title: Is The Quantum-Entangled Universe A Small World?
authors: Gregory S. Duane
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Partial entanglement may provide enough connections in the universe to satisfy the definition of a small world. To investigate this possibility, we define a network of particles on a given space-like hyper-surface with a long-range link between any two particles that are connected by a chain of exchanged particles involving less than some small maximum number of interactions. Considering the mean free paths of particles in different regions of space and the resulting probability distributions of entanglement connections vs. distance, we find evidence of small-world or random network structure on all but the smallest scales - corresponding to stars and planets - on which other types of connections would need to be added to complete the small world picture.
tldr: This paper explores whether partial entanglement between particles can form a network with small-world properties across cosmic scales.
motivation: To determine if the universe's entanglement structure resembles a small-world network, which could have implications for quantum gravity and cosmology.
method: The authors define a network of particles on a space-like hyper-surface, linking particles if they are connected through a short chain of interactions, and analyze the probability distributions of entanglement connections based on mean free paths.
result: Evidence suggests small-world or random network structure on all but the smallest scales such as stars and planets.
conclusion: Partial entanglement might make the universe a small world, but additional connection types may be necessary at small scales.

title: Fast Algorithms For Stoquastic Spin Systems
authors: Ryan L. Mann
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19489v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a general framework for developing fast sampling and counting algorithms for stoquastic spin systems at high temperature. Our framework is based on a rapidly mixing Markov chain for polymer models and a subcritical percolation process for sampling individual polymers. We apply our framework to obtain fast algorithms for approximating the partition function and sampling from the thermal distribution of (1) general stoquastic spin systems, (2) ferromagnetic Heisenberg models, and (3) antiferromagnetic Heisenberg models on bipartite graphs. For the Heisenberg models, we obtain an improved bound on the inverse temperature by using their respective cycle and loop representations.
tldr: This paper develops fast sampling and counting algorithms for stoquastic spin systems at high temperature using polymer models and percolation.
motivation: To efficiently approximate partition functions and sample from thermal states of stoquastic systems, which have applications in quantum computing and statistical physics.
method: Uses a rapidly mixing Markov chain for polymer models and a subcritical percolation process to sample individual polymers, applied to general stoquastic systems and Heisenberg models.
result: Provides fast algorithms with improved inverse temperature bounds for Heisenberg models using cycle and loop representations.
conclusion: Establishes a general framework for fast algorithms for stoquastic systems at high temperature.

title: Quantum Algorithm For Differential Equations Via Permutation Matrix Representation With Application To The Burgers Equation
authors: Hriday Sabharwal, Amir Kalev, Itay Hen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a quantum algorithm for solving the dynamics of the nonlinear viscous Burgers equation. We apply the Carleman linearization procedure on the spatially discretized equation, followed by a padding scheme that allows implementation on qubit registers. Existing Carleman-based quantum algorithms commonly formulate the lifted linear differential equation in an oracle model. Here we decompose the padded generator into diagonal masks and reversible arithmetic permutations using the Permutation Matrix Representation (PMR), which we show to be naturally compatible with the Linear Combination of Hamiltonian Simulations (LCHS) algorithm. Under the assumptions required by LCHS - most importantly positive semidefiniteness of the Hermitian part of the linear generator, possibly after a stabilizing shift - the algorithm prepares a normalized quantum state proportional to the solution of the truncated lifted system; the stabilizing shift introduces an exponential postselection overhead, which we quantify and mitigate through a rescaling scheme. We show that our algorithm scales with the off-diagonal norm of the Carleman generator instead of the matrix norm, which can be advantageous for other generators that are diagonally dominant. We also extend the PMR scheme to general fluid equations that may contain higher-order derivatives or nonlinear terms, or may involve multiple fluid variables or spatial dimensions. The construction illustrates how PMR can serve as a convenient Hamiltonian-simulation primitive for a broader class of LCU-based algorithms.
tldr: This paper develops a quantum algorithm for solving the viscous Burgers equation using Carleman linearization and permutation matrix representation, compatible with Linear Combination of Hamiltonian Simulations.
motivation: The goal is to create efficient quantum algorithms for nonlinear differential equations, using the Burgers equation as a benchmark for fluid dynamics.
method: The method spatially discretizes the equation, applies Carleman linearization to obtain a linear system, pads it for qubit registers, and decomposes the generator into diagonal masks and permutation matrices (PMR) for simulation via LCHS.
result: The algorithm scales with the off-diagonal norm of the Carleman generator, and the PMR scheme is extended to general fluid equations, potentially benefiting diagonally dominant generators.
conclusion: The PMR scheme serves as a convenient Hamiltonian-simulation primitive for LCU-based algorithms, but the stabilizing shift introduces exponential postselection overhead that can be mitigated.

title: Beyond Integrability Preserving Renormalization-Group Protocol In Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians With Time-Dependent Interaction Strengths
authors: Parameshwar R. Pasnoori
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is well established that in time-dependent quantum systems, integrability preserving time-dependent interaction strengths are identical to the renormalization group (RG) trajectories of the corresponding static model when time `[MATH]' in the driven model is identified with the logarithm of the cutoff `[MATH]' of the static model. We refer to this integrability preserving driving as the RG protocol. In this work we extend the class of time-dependent integrable models to include non-Hermitian quantum models with time-dependent interaction strengths. Using the recently formulated generalized Bethe ansatz framework [P. R. Pasnoori, Phys. Rev. B 112, L060409 (2025)], we show that the constraints imposed by integrability are more general: The interaction strengths of the static model that flow in the RG follow the respective RG trajectories in the corresponding time-dependent model as described above. In addition, the interaction strengths of the static model that are RG invariant can either be constant or have a specific time-dependence in the corresponding time-dependent model which is constrained by integrability. Thus we establish that in the context of time-dependent non-Hermitian systems, the set of integrability preserving time-dependent strengths is larger than the set corresponding to the RG protocol.
tldr: The paper extends integrability-preserving time-dependent driving to non-Hermitian Hamiltonians, showing that the constraints are broader than the RG protocol.
motivation: To generalize the RG protocol to non-Hermitian systems and explore more general integrable time-dependent models.
method: Uses the generalized Bethe ansatz framework to analyze time-dependent non-Hermitian integrable models.
result: Shows that interaction strengths that are RG invariant can have constant or specific time-dependence, leading to a larger set of integrable time-dependent strengths.
conclusion: Establishes that integrability-preserving time-dependent strengths are more general than the RG protocol in non-Hermitian contexts.

title: Variational Quantum Linear Solver Via Block Encoding For The Poisson Equation
authors: Viraj Dsouza, Ayush Singhal, Alex Khan, Rut Lineswala, Abhishek Chopra
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a variational quantum linear solver (VQLS) for the Poisson equation built on an exact block encoding of the discrete Laplacian, and demonstrate its performance on physically motivated benchmarks. Unlike LCU-based VQLS where the number of distinct circuits required per cost-function evaluation is [MATH], where [MATH] is the number of terms in the LCU decomposition of the discrete Laplacian operator, this approach requires only a single circuit for cost evaluation. We further empirically demonstrate that the choice of classical optimizer materially affects where the variational optimization ceases to make progress. The solver is benchmarked on three problems: a Poisson equation with sinusoidal forcing and a steady-state heat conduction problem with a localized Gaussian source, both with Dirichlet boundaries, and the pressure-Poisson equation of a two-dimensional lid-driven cavity flow, in which the solver is invoked once per time step under Neumann boundary conditions.
tldr: A variational quantum linear solver using exact block encoding of the discrete Laplacian for the Poisson equation, reducing circuit complexity and benchmarked on three problems.
motivation: To efficiently solve the Poisson equation on quantum computers, overcoming limitations of LCU-based VQLS which require many circuits.
method: Uses block encoding of the discrete Laplacian to require only a single circuit for cost evaluation, and empirically studies the effect of classical optimizer choice.
result: Benchmarked on three problems: sinusoidal forcing, heat conduction with Gaussian source, and lid-driven cavity flow, showing that optimizer choice affects convergence.
conclusion: The approach simplifies VQLS for Poisson equation and highlights the importance of optimizer selection.

title: A Layered Simplex Architecture For Large Alphabets
authors: Meir Feder, Yaniv Fogel, Ruediger Urbanke
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Probability estimation over large alphabets under log loss is a well-studied problem, with celebrated methods such as the Good-Turing estimator. We introduce and study a new Bayesian estimator with four notable properties. First, its construction is exceptionally simple: multiply independent uniform draws from the probability simplex coordinate-wise and renormalize. Depth is the only structural parameter, and averaging over depths eliminates the need to tune it. Second, the regret of the resulting mixture, the excess code length it pays relative to a code that knows the source, admits an explicit and efficiently computable expression. Third, despite its simplicity and lack of tuned constants, the estimator is competitive across a diverse set of synthetic and real-text benchmarks with substantially more specialized methods, including Good-Turing. Fourth, the tractability of its regret allows us to identify scaling laws in data, alphabet size, and depth. For Zipf targets with exponent above one, the regret has a simple reading as long as the sample reveals only a small fraction of the alphabet. It closely matches the description length of the set of discovered symbols, at one bit of code per bit of description, plus a further cost per symbol. The data exponent is therefore the rate at which new symbols are discovered.
tldr: Introduces a simple Bayesian estimator for probability estimation over large alphabets with explicit regret and competitive performance.
motivation: Probability estimation over large alphabets is crucial for coding and prediction, and existing methods like Good-Turing have limitations.
method: Proposes multiplying independent uniform draws from the probability simplex coordinate-wise and renormalizing, with depth as the only parameter, and averaging over depths.
result: The estimator has explicit and efficiently computable regret, is competitive with specialized methods, and reveals scaling laws.
conclusion: The simplicity and tractability make it a useful tool for large-alphabet probability estimation.

title: Redactable Blockchains And Polynomial Equations
authors: Alexander Demin, Alexey Ovchinnikov, Vladimir Shpilrain
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop new tools for constructing redactable authenticated data structures with post-quantum security. In our construction, inverting the proposed one-way function means solving a polynomial equation (or a system of polynomial equations) in more than one variable. This is presently considered quantum-safe, i.e., there is no known quantum algorithm that could solve this problem efficiently if parameters are chosen wisely.
tldr: This paper proposes a new construction for redactable blockchains using post-quantum one-way functions based on solving polynomial equations.
motivation: The goal is to develop authenticated data structures that remain secure against quantum attacks, specifically for redactable blockchains.
method: The authors design one-way functions whose inversion is equivalent to solving systems of polynomial equations, which is believed to be hard for quantum computers, and integrate them into a redactable blockchain framework.
result: The construction is argued to be quantum-safe, with security relying on the intractability of polynomial equation solving.
conclusion: The paper provides new tools for post-quantum secure redactable blockchains, but the work is focused on classical cryptographic protocols rather than quantum information theory or other listed research directions.

title: The Halo Engine: $\mathcal{O}(1)$-Step Compilation And Localized String Rupture For Lattice Gauge Theories On Quantum Hardware
authors: Abhiroop Gohar
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulating the real-time dynamics of lattice gauge theories (LGTs) represents a challenge for near-term quantum computing. Standard digital simulations rely on Trotterization schemes where circuit depth scales proportionally with lattice size, inevitably colliding with the coherence limits of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. To deal with this depth-scaling bottleneck, we introduce the Hardware-Aware Lattice Optimization (HALO) compiler, an architecture that executes global time-evolution steps in an immutable [MATH] circuit depth per Trotter step. Leveraging this framework, we elevate the digital simulation of the Quantum Link Model (QLM) truncation of the Schwinger model to the mesoscopic scale, utilizing a composite multi-qubit gauge link representation to support non-trivial electric field dynamics. We initialize and execute the non-perturbative dynamics of a heavily stretched [MATH] meson string on a 16-qubit superconducting transmon processor. By coupling the [MATH] compilation with Zero-Noise Extrapolation (ZNE), we suppress physical hardware decoherence to extract the precise dynamical crossover of localized pair creation, identifying the topological transition at [MATH] lattice units with an [MATH] rupture probability. Furthermore, we empirically map the dynamical phase diagram of the mesoscopic lattice, pinpointing the effective confinement phase boundary at precisely [MATH]. Finally, we extend the mathematical principles of the HALO engine to higher dimensions, presenting a scalable, constant-depth 2D unit-cell blueprint that eliminates the routing overhead of magnetic plaquettes, paving a direct algorithmic pathway toward the fault-tolerant simulation of two-dimensional Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD).
tldr: Introduces a constant-depth compiler for simulating lattice gauge theories on quantum hardware, demonstrated on a 16-qubit transmon.
motivation: Standard Trotterization depth scales with lattice size, limiting NISQ simulations; need for constant-depth compilation.
method: Proposes the HALO compiler achieving O(1) circuit depth per Trotter step, using composite multi-qubit gauge links and Zero-Noise Extrapolation.
result: Simulates the Schwinger model QLM on 16 qubits, identifying confinement phase boundary and topological transition with high probability.
conclusion: Presents a scalable blueprint for constant-depth simulation of 2D QCD, paving the way for fault-tolerant simulations.

title: Beyond Linear Subspaces: Nonlinear Moment Matching Meets Quadratic Manifolds
authors: Serkan Gugercin Reetish Padhi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quadratic manifold-based model order reduction offers a viable pathway to circumvent the limitations of linear subspaces for linear control systems characterized by slow Kolmogorov [MATH]-width decay. However, a system-theoretic framework for constructing such quadratic approximations remains absent from the literature. This paper presents a system-agnostic, optimization-free framework for the direct construction of quadratic projection matrices. We prove that the synthesized reduced-order model matches the nonlinear moments of the full-order system and preserves its exact center manifold mapping, thereby ensuring asymptotic tracking of steady-state outputs under specific input classes. Numerical results on transport-dominated benchmark problems, namely, the one-dimensional damped wave and advection equations, show that the proposed framework achieves high-fidelity trajectory reconstruction within a significantly reduced-dimensional state space, yielding substantial online computational savings.
tldr: This paper proposes a framework for constructing quadratic manifolds for model order reduction of linear control systems, achieving moment matching and center manifold preservation.
motivation: Linear subspace approximations fail for systems with slow Kolmogorov n-width decay; quadratic manifolds offer a viable alternative but lack a systematic construction framework.
method: The authors develop a system-agnostic, optimization-free method to construct quadratic projection matrices, ensuring the reduced model matches nonlinear moments and preserves exact center manifold mapping.
result: On benchmark problems (damped wave and advection), the method achieves high-fidelity trajectory reconstruction with significant computational savings in reduced dimensions.
conclusion: The proposed quadratic manifold framework provides a principled, non-iterative approach for model order reduction that overcomes limitations of linear subspaces.

title: Adaptive Time Windows For Discrete Adjoint Topology Optimization Of Unsteady Flows
authors: Zongyuan Liu, Kentaro Yaji, Musaddiq Al Ali, Shengfeng Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rather than prescribing an evaluation interval a priori, the proposed framework characterizes each evolving unsteady flow using a sequence of time windows. A consecutive-window convergence criterion is introduced to automatically identify a representative time window within its fully developed stage. The objective evaluation and discrete adjoint analysis are then carried out consistently over the identified representative time window. The framework is implemented using a regularized lattice Boltzmann method-based large-eddy simulation (LBM-LES) solver together with a partial bounce-back fluid-solid model. The consecutive-window convergence criterion is first validated using the backward-facing step flow. Cylinder-flow applications are then employed to investigate the influence of different flow regimes on the proposed framework. The wake-flow recovery problem verifies its effectiveness for unsteady topology optimization, while U-bend optimization further demonstrates its capability to identify and reorganize complex vortical structures.
tldr: This paper presents a framework for adaptive time window selection in discrete adjoint topology optimization of unsteady fluid flows.
motivation: To improve the efficiency and accuracy of topology optimization for unsteady flows by automatically determining the evaluation time window instead of prescribing it a priori.
method: The framework uses a consecutive-window convergence criterion to identify a representative time window in the fully developed stage, and employs a regularized lattice Boltzmann method-based large-eddy simulation (LBM-LES) solver with a partial bounce-back fluid-solid model.
result: The framework is validated on backward-facing step flow and cylinder-flow applications, and demonstrated on wake-flow recovery and U-bend optimization, showing its capability to identify and reorganize complex vortical structures.
conclusion: The adaptive time window approach is effective for unsteady topology optimization, providing a robust methodology for handling time-dependent flows.

title: Adaptive Error Budget Allocation For Fault-Tolerant Quantum Resource Estimation: A Metaheuristic Approach
authors: Tasnuva Farheen Asif Akhtab Ronggon
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: System-level resource estimation is a key component of fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) toolchains. Its efficiency depends on how global error tolerance is allocated across logical operations, T-state distillation, and rotation synthesis to minimize physical resource overhead. The commonly used uniform-allocation strategy ignores circuit-specific structure and can overprovision inactive or less critical subsystems, leading to inflated space-time estimates. Prior work aims to address this limitation using supervised models trained on offline-generated datasets. However, this approach incurs additional data-generation costs and limits deployment flexibility. To overcome these drawbacks, we propose a training-free optimization framework that performs derivative-free search directly on the Azure Quantum Resource Estimator (AQRE), enabling instance-specific error budget allocation for previously unseen circuits without requiring offline training data. To evaluate robustness to optimizer choice, we instantiate the framework with two structurally distinct metaheuristics, simulated annealing and quantum particle swarm optimization. We evaluate our framework across 433 circuits spanning 2 to 91 qubits from 31 families in the MQT Bench suite. Across the benchmark suite, both methods reduce space-time cost by more than 33\% on average and agree within 1.34\% points, indicating that the gains are stable across different metaheuristic search strategies. Our analysis further finds that the optimization benefit is driven primarily by error-profile asymmetry rather than circuit scale, and the metric, Gini coefficient of optimized allocation, provides an interpretable diagnostic of expected improvement. Together, these results position adaptive error budget allocation as a system-software optimization layer for FTQC resource estimation pipeline.
tldr: A training-free optimization framework using metaheuristics for adaptive error budget allocation in fault-tolerant quantum resource estimation, reducing space-time cost by over 33% on benchmark circuits.
motivation: Uniform error budget allocation in FTQC resource estimation is inefficient, and supervised approaches require expensive offline data generation.
method: The framework uses simulated annealing and quantum particle swarm optimization to perform derivative-free search directly on the Azure Quantum Resource Estimator, allocating error budgets per circuit instance.
result: On 433 circuits from MQT Bench, both methods reduce space-time cost by more than 33% on average, agree within 1.34% points, and the benefit is driven by error-profile asymmetry.
conclusion: Adaptive error budget allocation via metaheuristics is a practical system-software optimization layer for FTQC resource estimation pipelines.

title: Exact Expressions Of Correlation Functions Between Two Spins In The Boundary Row Of The Two-dimensional Rectangular Ising Model With Periodic-free Boundary Conditions And Finite Size
authors: Mei Tao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present exact expressions of correlation functions between two spins in the boundary row of the two-dimensional rectangular Ising model with periodic-free boundary conditions and finite size. Some properties of exact expressions obtained are discussed. The fundamental property of the Ising model that the long range order emerge as the temperature decrease is shown clearly; expressions of the correlation functions in the thermodynamic limit varies depending on the order of taking limits of two parameters L and N; the impact of different sizes on correlation functions is illustrated with the aid of diagrams. Expressions of the correlation function discussed in this paper in the thermodynamic limit has been presented by previous researchers, and we prove that expressions obtained in this article is identical in form to expressions provided by previous researchers in the thermodynamic limit.
tldr: 该论文研究了二维矩形Ising模型边界行自旋关联函数的精确表达式，属于经典统计力学领域，与量子信息研究方向无关。
motivation: 经典Ising模型是统计物理的经典模型，作者旨在推导有限尺寸下边界行关联函数的精确表达式，并探讨其性质。
method: 作者使用数学方法推导了二维矩形Ising模型在周期性-自由边界条件下的关联函数精确表达式，并验证了热力学极限下与已有结果的一致性。
result: 获得了有限尺寸下边界行自旋关联函数的精确表达式，展示了长程序随温度降低的出现，并讨论了不同尺寸的影响。
conclusion: 该研究属于经典统计物理，与量子信息、量子热力学等研究方向无直接关联。

title: Dataflows And Computational Patterns For Hybrid Quantum-Classical Scientific Computing
authors: Ryan Landfield, Jordan J. Winetrout, Michael A. Sandoval
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical computing has emerged as the dominant paradigm for near-term quantum applications, yet hybrid workflows are typically described by individual algorithms rather than their underlying execution behavior. We introduce the Quantum Execution Locality Framework (QELF), a qualitative framework for characterizing hybrid quantum-classical workflows according to recurring dataflow structures and quantum execution locality, the extent to which computation remains resident on the Quantum Processing Unit (QPU) before host intervention or classical synchronization. From a representative cross-section of applications, QELF identifies five recurring computational patterns with distinct locality characteristics and discusses their implications for communication overhead, workflow organization, and future hybrid computing architectures. By providing a common vocabulary for reasoning about hybrid workloads, QELF establishes a foundation for future quantitative validation and the co-design of algorithms, runtime systems, and hybrid computing architectures.
tldr: A qualitative framework (QELF) for characterizing hybrid quantum-classical workflows by dataflow structures and execution locality.
motivation: Hybrid workflows are typically described by individual algorithms, lacking a common vocabulary to reason about their execution behavior and design future architectures.
method: The authors propose the Quantum Execution Locality Framework (QELF) based on a cross-section of applications, identifying five recurring computational patterns with distinct locality characteristics.
result: QELF provides a taxonomy of hybrid workflows and discusses implications for communication overhead, workflow organization, and future hybrid computing architectures.
conclusion: The framework establishes a foundation for quantitative validation and co-design of algorithms, runtime systems, and hybrid architectures.

title: Black-Box Coherence Matrix Eigen-Spectroscopy With Programmable Photonics
authors: Kevin Zelaya, Jonathan Friedman, Mohammad-Ali Miri
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The precise characterization of spatial optical coherence is fundamental to emerging applications in optical communications and computational imaging. However, extracting the full coherence matrix traditionally requires phase-sensitive interferometry, which is highly vulnerable to environmental noise and poses severe scalability challenges for integrated photonics. Here, we introduce an architecture-agnostic framework for analyzing and controlling partially coherent light on programmable photonic circuits. By leveraging the Schur-Horn theorem, our approach systematically diagonalizes the incident coherence matrix, relying solely on output intensity measurements and entirely circumventing the need for complex phase retrieval. We experimentally validate this black-box protocol on a low-depth, non-universal photonic integrated circuit, successfully reconstructing the hidden eigenvalues of mixed states generated from up to four mutually incoherent sources. Furthermore, we demonstrate active, in-situ statistical light control by introducing non-unitary amplitude modulation to significantly enhance interference visibility, exposing a fundamental physical trade-off between coherence enhancement and optical loss. Inherently resilient to hardware constraints and experimental noise, this scalable paradigm establishes a robust pathway for realizing ultra-compact, on-chip spatial coherence analyzers.
tldr: A framework for characterizing spatial optical coherence using programmable photonic circuits, based on the Schur-Horn theorem and intensity-only measurements, with experimental validation.
motivation: Precise characterization of spatial optical coherence is crucial for optical communications and imaging, but traditional phase-sensitive interferometry is noise-prone and not scalable for integrated photonics.
method: The authors use the Schur-Horn theorem to diagonalize the incident coherence matrix using only output intensity measurements, avoiding phase retrieval, and implement this on a low-depth, non-universal photonic integrated circuit.
result: Experimentally reconstructed hidden eigenvalues of mixed states from up to four mutually incoherent sources, and demonstrated active statistical light control via non-unitary amplitude modulation, revealing a trade-off between coherence enhancement and optical loss.
conclusion: The scalable, noise-resilient approach offers a robust path for ultra-compact on-chip spatial coherence analyzers.

title: Renormalization Group Ontology In Quantum Foundations: A Non-interacting Spin-0 Toy Model
authors: Gary Kapilevich
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A realist, anti-psi interpretation of quantum field theory is introduced, based on an expanded ontology that was inspired by the renormalization group. A goal will be to work with a classical non-interacting scalar field "toy model" in the canonical ensemble and show that an observer in this expanded ontology, under certain limiting conditions, will see a QFT. The inverse renormalization group (IRG) will be key in both interpreting this expanded ontology and furnishing novel examples of QFTs. This will lead to a definition of Planck's constant that flows as we head towards a fixed point, is expressed in terms of a temperature, and depends on the observer being studied in this expanded ontology. Our hope is that this approach will lead both to insights into quantum foundations and to prescriptions for developing new QFTs.
tldr: A paper proposing a realist interpretation of quantum field theory using renormalization group concepts, with a classical toy model to derive QFT from an expanded ontology.
motivation: To provide a novel interpretation of quantum foundations, potentially leading to new QFTs.
method: Uses a classical non-interacting scalar field in canonical ensemble, applies inverse renormalization group, and defines Planck's constant as a flowing quantity dependent on temperature and observer.
result: Shows that under certain limits, an observer in this ontology sees a QFT, providing a new perspective on quantum field theory.
conclusion: Suggests that this approach may offer insights into quantum foundations and prescriptions for developing new QFTs.

title: Which Pulse Maximizes Resonant Nonlinear Conversion?
authors: Alex Krasnok
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At fixed pulse energy, which drive waveform extracts the most [MATH]th-order nonlinear conversion from a resonator ([MATH] for second harmonic)? A short pulse couples poorly to a narrow resonance, a long one dilutes its energy, and no linear rule fixes the compromise. We solve the problem exactly for a single mode of amplitude decay rate [MATH]. Eliminating the drive turns fixed incident energy into a constraint on the stored field alone, and the optimization becomes a sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality whose extremal is the ground-state soliton of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation. The optimal stored field is [MATH], sustained by an asymmetric input that rises as [MATH] and falls as [MATH]; the largest converted energy follows in closed form. A rising exponential, the time-reversal recipe, retains at most [MATH] of the bound at [MATH] and [MATH] at large [MATH]; a two-rate pulse retains above [MATH]. Critical coupling generalizes to [MATH]-fold overcoupling, with optimal input coupling [MATH] times the intrinsic loss rate. The bound applies from microrings to superconducting circuits and caps the per-pulse brightness of broadband photon-pair sources.
tldr: This paper analytically determines the optimal pulse shape for maximizing nth-order nonlinear conversion in a resonator at fixed pulse energy, yielding a closed-form solution.
motivation: The need to efficiently convert laser pulses to higher harmonics in resonators, where pulse duration must balance coupling and energy dilution.
method: The optimization is recast as a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality, solved via the nonlinear Schrödinger equation, giving an extremal solitonic solution.
result: The optimal stored field is a bright soliton with asymmetric input, achieving higher conversion than standard exponential or two-rate pulses; critical coupling becomes n-fold overcoupling.
conclusion: The derived bound provides a fundamental limit on per-pulse conversion efficiency across various resonator platforms, with implications for photon-pair source brightness.

title: Statistical Complexity From Fluctuations In The Information Content
authors: Renio S. Mendes, Sergio Picoli, Evaldo M. F. Curado
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We argue that the variance of the information content ([MATH]), an information-theoretic quantity, can be naturally interpreted as a measure of statistical complexity. We show that [MATH] satisfies widely accepted criteria for statistical complexity measures: it vanishes for both ordered and equiprobable states, while attaining maxima in intermediate regimes, typically shifted toward order. This interpretation establishes direct connections with thermodynamics and phase transitions: for systems obeying Boltzmann--Gibbs statistics, [MATH] is extensive and directly proportional to energy fluctuations and heat capacity. Moreover, unlike other statistical complexity measures, it attains a maximum at continuous phase transitions, as illustrated for the two-dimensional Ising model. Applications to chaotic maps and fractional Gaussian noise further indicate that [MATH] captures nontrivial dynamical structure in different classes of correlated systems.
tldr: The paper proposes the variance of information content as a measure of statistical complexity, linking it to thermodynamics and phase transitions.
motivation: To introduce a new statistical complexity measure that satisfies standard criteria and has direct thermodynamic interpretations, particularly connecting to energy fluctuations and heat capacity.
method: The authors analyze the properties of the variance of information content, show it vanishes for ordered and equiprobable states, and derive its relationship to thermodynamic quantities for Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics. They test it on the 2D Ising model, chaotic maps, and fractional Gaussian noise.
result: The measure meets criteria for complexity, is extensive and proportional to heat capacity, and attains a maximum at continuous phase transitions.
conclusion: The variance of information content is a useful complexity measure with thermodynamic significance, capable of capturing nontrivial structure in correlated systems.

title: Variational Quantum Circuit Parameterization Of SchNet: A Simulator-Based Feasibility Study For Conservative Molecular Force Fields
authors: Hoang - Anh Nguyen, Nhu - Duc Dinh, Viet - Hung Tran, Tu - Uyen Le Tu, Tien - Lam Pham, van - Duy Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learning force fields provide a promising route for accelerating molecular simulation by replacing expensive quantum-chemical calculations with differentiable models of molecular energies and atomic forces. However, learning accurate and energy-conserving forces remains challenging, especially when the model must capture both global energy trends and local potential-energy gradients from limited data. In this work, we propose a Hybrid Quantum SchNet architecture that integrates variational quantum circuit modules into the continuous-filter SchNet framework. Quantum modules are inserted into the filter generator, atom-wise update, and readout transformations, allowing quantum-enhanced feature mappings to contribute to distance-dependent interactions and atomic energy prediction while preserving the energy-gradient formulation of forces. The model is evaluated on eight MD17 molecular systems using 1000 training configurations per molecule. Compared with energy-only training, joint energy--force supervision substantially improves both energy and force prediction accuracy. Compared with energy-only training, joint energy--force supervision substantially improves both energy and force prediction accuracy. Averaged over the benchmark, the energy MAE decreases from 2.567 to 0.593 kcal mol[MATH], while the force MAE decreases from 16.340 to 1.540 kcal mol[MATH] \AA[MATH]. Ablation experiments on ethanol further show that the performance of the hybrid model depends on the balance between quantum circuit width, circuit depth, and optimization stability. These results demonstrate that variational quantum circuits can be incorporated into neural force-field architectures and trained end-to-end to improve molecular energy and force prediction.
tldr: This paper integrates variational quantum circuits into the SchNet neural network for molecular force field prediction, achieving improved accuracy with joint energy-force training.
motivation: Machine-learning force fields need to capture both global energy trends and local gradients from limited data; quantum-enhanced feature mappings may improve accuracy and energy conservation.
method: The Hybrid Quantum SchNet architecture inserts variational quantum circuit modules into the filter generator, atom-wise update, and readout transformations, preserving the energy-gradient formulation. It is trained on eight MD17 molecules with 1000 configurations each, comparing energy-only vs joint energy-force supervision.
result: Joint training reduces energy MAE from 2.567 to 0.593 kcal/mol and force MAE from 16.340 to 1.540 kcal/mol/Å on average; ablation studies on ethanol show performance depends on quantum circuit width, depth, and optimization stability.
conclusion: Variational quantum circuits can be effectively integrated into neural force-field architectures and trained end-to-end to improve molecular energy and force predictions.

title: Exact Partition Function Of Arithmetic Ising Model
authors: Anu Dhochak, Ken Kikuchi, Shrinit Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a compact formula for the exact partition function of the [MATH]-dimensional arithmetic Ising model (AIM). For a [MATH] system, we express it analytically using the [MATH]-Hurwitz-Lerch zeta function and derive explicit forms for the free energy and entropy. Additionally, we find that the entropy increases at high temperatures, supporting the presence of entropic order.
tldr: The paper presents an exact formula for the partition function of the arithmetic Ising model using the Hurwitz-Lerch zeta function, and derives expressions for free energy and entropy, finding that entropy increases at high temperatures, indicating entropic order.
motivation: To obtain exact analytical solutions for thermodynamic quantities of a specific classical spin model, which may reveal non-trivial ordering phenomena and mathematical insights.
method: The authors use the generalized Hurwitz-Lerch zeta function to express the partition function exactly, and from it derive the free energy and entropy analytically.
result: The entropy increases at high temperatures, supporting the presence of entropic order in the arithmetic Ising model.
conclusion: The exact partition function provides a compact analytical description of the model's thermodynamics and highlights the role of entropic ordering.

title: Moore--Read Construction And Explicit Monodromies Of Laughlin States On Riemann Surfaces
authors: Kiyoon Eum
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the Moore--Read construction of the [MATH] Laughlin states on compact Riemann surfaces, deriving their conformal blocks from [MATH] Chern--Simons theory through the CS/WZW correspondence. We compute their explicit monodromies under quasi-hole transport and Aharonov--Bohm flux insertion, and conjecture that these coincide with the corresponding adiabatic holonomies. Under this identification, we recover classical results on Laughlin states including the flux-averaged Hall conductance [MATH] via a vector bundle of Laughlin states over [MATH]. We also relate our construction to the recently developed algebro-geometric approach to higher genus Laughlin states.
tldr: This paper revisits the Moore-Read construction of Laughlin states on compact Riemann surfaces via Chern-Simons theory, computes their explicit monodromies, and conjectures these equal adiabatic holonomies, recovering Hall conductance.
motivation: To provide explicit monodromies for Laughlin states and connect the construction to algebro-geometric approaches, thereby unifying different frameworks.
method: The authors use the Chern-Simons/Wess-Zumino-Witten correspondence to derive conformal blocks and compute monodromies under quasi-hole transport and flux insertion.
result: They compute explicit monodromies, conjecture their equivalence to adiabatic holonomies, and recover the flux-averaged Hall conductance, while linking to higher genus Laughlin state constructions.
conclusion: The construction provides a systematic way to compute monodromies and holonomies for Laughlin states, with implications for understanding anyonic statistics in fractional quantum Hall systems.

title: Assembly Theory And The Smallest Grammar Problem
authors: Wawrzyniec Bieniawski
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assembly theory (AT) quantifies complexity through the assembly index (ASI) -- a metric proven equivalent to the size of the smallest straight-line program (SLP). While this equivalence links AT to data compression -- a field shaped by decades of research -- the practical efficacy of specific algorithms as ASI approximators remains largely unexplored. This study provides an empirical evaluation of eight compression algorithms, spanning grammar-based and dictionary schemes (CAs) across a dataset of 408 strings -- comprising 368 synthetic strings (including max-complexity strings and strings with varying levels of symbol distribution balance, quantified by Shannon entropy) and 40 natural biological sequences (genomic and proteomic). We introduce Re-Pair T-NDR, a branch-and-bound tie-resolving variant of Re-Pair, providing a tighter upper bound on the ASI than the other CAs researched in this study. Increasing alphabet size extends the regime in which CAs closely track the ASI, delaying a ``divergence point'', where a CA deviates from the optimal assembly path. The results establish compression algorithms as practical tools for ASI estimation.
tldr: This paper empirically evaluates eight compression algorithms as approximators of the assembly index, a complexity metric equivalent to the smallest straight-line program.
motivation: To understand the practical efficacy of compression algorithms in estimating assembly complexity, bridging assembly theory with data compression.
method: They benchmark eight grammar-based and dictionary compression algorithms on 408 strings (synthetic and biological) and introduce a tie-resolving variant of Re-Pair.
result: The Re-Pair T-NDR variant provides the tightest upper bound on assembly index; larger alphabets extend the regime where algorithms track the optimal assembly path.
conclusion: Compression algorithms are practical tools for assembly index estimation, with implications for complexity quantification.

title: The Second Edge Theorem: The Asymptotic Collapse Of Sample-Dependent Information Geometry To The Canonical Flat Canvas Of Conventional Statistics In Large Sample Limits
authors: Bing Cheng, Yi-Shuai Niu, Howell Tong, Shing-Tung Yau
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes the global proof of the Second Edge Theorem: as sample size tends to infinity, sample-dependent information-geometric manifolds---formed by the parameter space, sample-scaled Fisher metric, and dual alpha-connections---undergo metric-topological collapse onto the flat tangent space of Conventional Statistics at the true parameter. We first prove a universal tensor valence scaling law, under which tensor fields of valence one through four degenerate at rates determined by sample size. Score fluctuations stabilize, the Fisher metric freezes to its true-parameter value, affine connections dissolve, and Riemann curvature is annihilated. We then bridge geometric collapse with statistical decision theory, showing that Cheeger--Gromov flattening and Le Cam risk condensation are dual projections of the same asymptotic phase transition. A Fisher-compatible Ehresmann connection extends these results to over-parameterized and singular models, yielding horizontal leaf-space collapse and uniform local asymptotic normality. Unifying the First and Second Edge Theorems yields a nested dual-edge hierarchy: Conventional Statistics is the boundary of Information Geometry, which is itself the boundary of Statistical Mechanics and Geometry. Thus, Conventional Statistics is not a heuristic approximation but the unique zero-curvature thermodynamic attractor of regular parametric information manifolds. This redefines modern statistics as a dynamic non-equilibrium field theory of finite-sample fluctuations, phase transitions, and gauge-invariant interactions.
tldr: Proves that sample-dependent information geometry collapses to flat conventional statistics in large sample limits, establishing a hierarchy where conventional statistics is the boundary of information geometry.
motivation: To understand the asymptotic behavior of information-geometric manifolds and their connection to conventional statistics and statistical mechanics.
method: Introduces a tensor valence scaling law and uses Cheeger–Gromov flattening and Le Cam risk condensation to show geometric collapse.
result: The collapse occurs, unifying statistical decision theory and information geometry, with a nested hierarchy: conventional statistics as boundary of information geometry, itself a boundary of statistical mechanics.
conclusion: Conventional statistics is the unique zero-curvature thermodynamic attractor of regular parametric information manifolds.

title: Information Geometry (ig) Lives At Edge Or Boundary Of Smg (statistically Meaningful Geometry): - The First Edge Theorem And Applications
authors: Bing Cheng, Yi-Shuai Niu, Howell Tong, Shing-Tung Yau
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Statistically Meaningful Geometry (SMG) is a differential-geometric and information-theoretic framework that lifts over-parameterized models into infinite-dimensional non-parametric Orlicz statistical fiber bundles with an Ehresmann connection, decoupling unobservable vertical gauge noise from horizontal statistically verifiable directions. We prove the First Edge Theorem: Amari's information geometry (IG) and conventional statistics (CS) are not autonomous statistical universes but degenerate boundary layers of the larger gauge-active SMG space. Taking the structural identifiability radius [MATH] breaks gauge symmetry, collapses vertical fibers, and forces the total space onto the IG manifold; subsequent local asymptotic normality as [MATH] flattens the remaining curvature, yielding \[ . \] The same fiber-bundle machinery transforms model non-identifiability from a singular collapse into a structured gauge space. Applications include resolving the deep-learning generalization paradox, constructing gauge-invariant gradient descent and holonomy-matched preference alignment for generative AI, and solving weak identification in structural econometrics via intrinsic horizontal geodesic search.
tldr: The paper proves the First Edge Theorem, showing that Amari's information geometry and conventional statistics are boundary layers of a larger gauge-active statistically meaningful geometric (SMG) framework, with applications to deep learning and econometrics.
motivation: To unify and extend classical information geometry and statistics within a differential-geometric framework, addressing model non-identifiability and other longstanding issues.
method: Introduces an infinite-dimensional non-parametric Orlicz statistical fiber bundle with an Ehresmann connection, decoupling vertical gauge noise from horizontal statistical directions, and uses gauge symmetry breaking and local asymptotic normality to derive the Edge Theorem.
result: Establishes that standard information geometry and conventional statistics emerge as degenerate limits of the SMG framework, and demonstrates applications to deep learning generalization, gauge-invariant gradient descent, and weak identification in econometrics.
conclusion: The SMG framework provides a structured view of model non-identifiability and offers new tools for machine learning and statistical inference, but is not relevant to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Minimum Attaining Operators On Reducing Subspaces: Spectral Structure And Density
authors: Golla Ramesh Puspendu Nag
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we introduce and investigate a new subclass [MATH] of minimum attaining operators on a separable Hilbert space [MATH]. This class contains the absolutely minimum attaining operators and is properly contained in the class of minimum attaining operators. We establish several structural and spectral characterizations of operators in [MATH]. In particular, we characterize positive operators in [MATH] in terms of their spectral representations. We prove that [MATH] is dense in [MATH] in the operator norm and, moreover, that the operators in [MATH] having a nontrivial invariant half-space are also dense in [MATH] in the operator norm. We further obtain a representation theorem for normal operators in [MATH] and establish additional structural properties of this class.
tldr: This paper introduces and studies a new subclass of minimum attaining operators on Hilbert spaces, providing structural and spectral characterizations and demonstrating density results.
motivation: To understand the structure and properties of minimum attaining operators, possibly for applications in operator theory and spectral analysis.
method: The paper defines the subclass, derives spectral representations for positive operators, proves density in the operator norm, and obtains representation theorems for normal operators.
result: Establishes characterizations for operators in the class, shows the class is dense in the operator norm, and that operators with invariant half-spaces are also dense.
conclusion: The new subclass lies between absolutely minimum attaining and minimum attaining operators, with rich structural properties.

title: Hodge Coercivity And Global Dynamics In Two-Field Edge-Cochain Systems With MHD-Type Cancellation
authors: Moses Boudourides
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A finite-dimensional two-field system for divergence-free edge cochains is introduced. Its MHD-type designation refers only to a quadratic exchange pattern and exact total-energy cancellation; it is not a physical MHD discretization. A general cancellation class is separated from a corrected explicit realization: the anticommutator [MATH] is skew-symmetric for diagonal [MATH] and skew-symmetric [MATH], and its projected bilinear map has the required trilinear antisymmetry. The central result is a Hodge coercivity criterion: the full divergence-free space admits the Poincar\'e-type estimate needed for dissipativity if and only if its harmonic [MATH]-cochain space is trivial. Under this condition, global existence, an exact energy identity, an absorbing ball, and a compact global attractor follow. When harmonic modes are present, a harmonic-decoupled interaction class yields invariant harmonic affine fibres and fibre-wise attractors. Deterministic disk, annular, and two-hole examples illustrate the spectral criterion, energy law, and distinction between general harmonic exchange and harmonic-fibre invariance.
tldr: This paper analyzes a finite-dimensional two-field edge-cochain system with MHD-type cancellation, establishing Hodge coercivity conditions for global dynamics and attractors.
motivation: To understand the global dynamics and dissipativity of a mathematical model inspired by MHD, using discrete calculus on edge cochains.
method: Introduces a two-field system with divergence-free edge cochains, studies Hodge coercivity via harmonic cochain space, and analyzes energy cancellation and bilinear map antisymmetry.
result: Proves that the divergence-free space admits the needed Poincaré-type estimate iff harmonic cochain space is trivial, leading to global existence, energy identity, absorbing ball, and global attractor; harmonic modes lead to invariant fibres and fibre-wise attractors.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous mathematical framework for such systems, with examples illustrating the criteria.

title: Resolving The Generalized Hyperbolicity Conjecture For Shadowing
authors: Mih\'aly Pituk
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is known that generalized hyperbolicity implies the shadowing property for invertible bounded linear operators on a Banach space. Whether the converse holds has been a central open problem in linear dynamics and has been conjectured to have a positive answer. We show that this conjecture fails on general Banach spaces by constructing a counterexample, whereas it holds on separable Hilbert spaces. The distinction is explained by the gap that may occur on Banach spaces between surjectivity and right invertibility, a gap that disappears on Hilbert spaces. The main ingredients of the proofs are a recent spectral characterization of shadowing in terms of the surjective spectrum and a new characterization of generalized hyperbolicity in terms of right resolvent functions near the unit circle.
tldr: The paper resolves the generalized hyperbolicity conjecture for shadowing, showing it fails on general Banach spaces but holds on separable Hilbert spaces.
motivation: A central open problem in linear dynamics asks whether the shadowing property implies generalized hyperbolicity for invertible bounded linear operators; prior work proved the reverse implication only.
method: The author constructs a counterexample on a general Banach space and proves the positive result on separable Hilbert spaces, using a spectral characterization of shadowing and a new characterization of generalized hyperbolicity via right resolvent functions.
result: The conjecture fails on general Banach spaces but holds on separable Hilbert spaces, with the distinction attributed to the gap between surjectivity and right invertibility.
conclusion: The gap between surjectivity and right invertibility on Banach spaces explains the failure of the conjecture, and the new characterizations provide insight into the relationship between shadowing and hyperbolicity.

title: Nonexistence Of Frame Measures For Separated Uniform Consecutive-Digit Bernoulli Convolutions
authors: Wei-Jie Wang Xiao-Ye Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the existence problem of frame measures for uniform consecutive-digit Bernoulli convolutions under the separated scaling condition. Given parameters [MATH] and [MATH], we prove that if [MATH] for some integers [MATH] and [MATH], with [MATH], then the associated [MATH]-Bernoulli convolution [MATH] admits no frame measure. The proof introduces a new cyclic mask-quotient obstruction adapted to the multi-character structure of the consecutive-digit framework.

motivation: To determine whether certain self-similar fractal measures admit frame measures, which are important for stable reconstruction in sampling theory.
method: The proof introduces a cyclic mask-quotient obstruction adapted to the multi-character structure of consecutive-digit Bernoulli convolutions.

title: Learning Deterministic And Stochastic Forced Hamiltonian Systems
authors: Tomasz Tyranowski Benedikt Brantner
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a geometric framework for learning deterministic and stochastic forced Hamiltonian systems with neural networks. Motivated by the Lagrange-d'Alembert principle and the theory of variational integrators, we introduce the notion of a Lagrange-d'Alembert map and establish a [MATH] convergence theorem for first-order one-step methods. Building on these results, we propose Generalized Forced Hamiltonian Neural Networks (GFHNNs), a class of structure-preserving neural networks obtained by concatenating Lagrange-d'Alembert-Euler maps, and prove a universal approximation theorem for this architecture. We further extend the framework to parameter-dependent systems, leading to Parametric Generalized Forced Hamiltonian Neural Networks (PGFHNNs). By interpreting the multiple Stratonovich integrals appearing in the Stratonovich-Taylor expansion as parameters, the same framework can be applied to stochastic forced Hamiltonian systems whenever information about the underlying Wiener process is available. Our numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed geometric architectures provide significantly improved long-time stability and accuracy compared to non-geometric residual neural networks, while requiring substantially less training data to achieve a comparable level of performance.
tldr: The paper introduces a geometric framework for learning deterministic and stochastic forced Hamiltonian systems with neural networks, proposing structure-preserving architectures (GFHNNs and PGFHNNs) that improve long-time stability and data efficiency.
motivation: Standard neural networks often lack long-time stability and require large amounts of data when modeling Hamiltonian systems; incorporating geometric structure can address these issues.
method: The authors define Lagrange-d'Alembert maps based on the Lagrange-d'Alembert principle and variational integrators, then compose these maps to build Generalized Forced Hamiltonian Neural Networks. They also extend the framework to stochastic systems via Stratonovich integrals and parametric versions.
result: They prove convergence and universal approximation theorems, and numerical experiments demonstrate significantly improved accuracy and stability with less training data compared to non-geometric residual networks.
conclusion: Structure-preserving neural networks based on geometric integration principles are effective for learning deterministic and stochastic Hamiltonian dynamics, offering practical advantages in simulation and modeling.

title: Tri-Hybrid Beamforming For T-RIS-Enabled Base Station
authors: Chenlong Ding Hongtao Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (T-RISs) integrated into the transmitter provide a viable realization of tri-hybrid multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO), where spatial processing is distributed across the digital, analog radio-frequency (RF), and electromagnetic (EM) domains. However, unlike conventional RIS-assisted links, a transmitter-native T-RIS directly participates in radiation formation, making T-RIS front-end modeling and weighted sum-rate (WSR)-oriented joint precoding challenging under practical hardware constraints. This paper develops a unified modeling and precoding framework for transmitter-native T-RIS tri-hybrid multi-user (MU) downlink transmission. Specifically, starting from a continuous-field description, the received field is characterized by the interaction among the feed array, the programmable T-RIS aperture, and the user-side propagation, leading to a cascaded baseband input-output model for MU precoding. Furthermore, the same representation is instantiated in the Fresnel, Fraunhofer, and mixed-field regimes, so that near-field focusing and far-field angular steering can be handled within one front-end model. Additionally, a WSR maximization problem is formulated over the digital precoder, analog network, and T-RIS coefficients under power and quantization constraints. A two-level solver is then developed by coupling outer weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE) updates with WMMSE-induced aperture-field shaping and hardware projection. Simulations validate the modeling accuracy and convergence, and show that the proposed full tri-hybrid design improves WSR over baselines while suppressing mixed-field cross-regime leakage.
tldr: This paper presents a unified modeling and precoding framework for tri-hybrid MIMO systems using transmitter-native transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (T-RIS) to maximize weighted sum-rate in multi-user downlink.
motivation: Conventional RIS-assisted links differ because transmitter-native T-RIS directly participates in radiation formation, making modeling and precoding challenging under hardware constraints.
method: They develop a cascaded baseband input-output model from continuous-field description, instantiate it for near-field and far-field regimes, formulate a WSR maximization problem over digital precoder, analog network, and T-RIS coefficients under power and quantization constraints, and solve it with a two-level solver coupling outer WMMSE updates with aperture-field shaping and hardware projection.
result: Simulations validate modeling accuracy and convergence, showing the full tri-hybrid design improves WSR over baselines while suppressing mixed-field cross-regime leakage.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides an effective design for T-RIS-enabled base stations, achieving performance gains in multi-user scenarios.

title: A Controllability Gramain Shaping With Lmi Constraints Under Bures--Wasserstein Distance
authors: Koju Nishimoto, Yuki Onishi, Riku Funada, Mitsuji Sampei
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a controller design method for shaping the controllability Gramian into a desired form to design the effect from exogenous inputs to the system state. Using the Bures--Wasserstein distance, we formulate the shaping problem as the minimization of the distance between the system Gramian and a desired Gramian, and the objective function is shown to be strictly convex on the set of symmetric positive definite matrices. In addition, by deriving a semidefinite programming formulation via a linear matrix inequality (LMI), computational efficiency is improved and additional LMI constraints can be incorporated. When the exogenous input is modeled as Gaussian white noise, the proposed framework is closely related to [MATH] control, which can be interpreted as a special case of optimal transport. Numerical examples demonstrate anisotropic controllability design for a guidance robot and verify the ability to impose additional directional constraints through LMIs. The numerical examples also confirm that the proposed method approaches [MATH] control as the desired Gramian tends to zero.
tldr: This paper proposes a controller design method to shape the controllability Gramian using the Bures–Wasserstein distance and LMI constraints, enabling anisotropic control design.
motivation: The authors aim to design the effect of exogenous inputs on system states by shaping the controllability Gramian into a desired form, which is a classical control problem.
method: The shaping problem is formulated as minimizing the Bures–Wasserstein distance between the system Gramian and a desired Gramian, and is transformed into a semidefinite programming via LMI constraints.
result: Numerical examples demonstrate anisotropic controllability design for a guidance robot and verify the ability to impose directional constraints through LMIs, also confirming convergence to H-infinity control as the desired Gramian tends to zero.
conclusion: The proposed framework is computationally efficient and allows additional LMI constraints, providing a practical approach for controllability shaping that connects to optimal transport and H-infinity control.

title: Learning Piecewise-smooth Dynamical Systems
authors: Davide Murari, Erik Jansson, Chris Budd OBE, Carola-Bibiane Sch\"onlieb
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discovering dynamical systems from trajectory data is a central problem in applied mathematics and engineering. Whilst recent advances in machine learning have led to strong progress in data-driven system identification, much less attention has been given to systems with discontinuous dynamics. These systems are nevertheless highly relevant in applications, including climate dynamics and mechanical systems with friction. In this work, we consider the problem of identifying piecewise-smooth dynamical systems directly from trajectory data. Compared with the smooth setting, this requires recovering the governing equations and detecting the switching hyperplanes that separate different dynamical regimes and characterising their behaviour, such as sliding motion. We present a modular framework for discovering such systems by first estimating switching hyperplanes from data and then learning smooth dynamics within each region using geometry-constrained neural networks. The geometry-learning phase is studied from a statistical perspective, analysing the identifiability of the discontinuities and the robustness of the procedure. We also introduce a novel neural network architecture with a prescribed discontinuity set, and provide a theoretical analysis of its approximation properties. The approach is tested on low-dimensional benchmark problems, including dry-friction oscillators and the PP04 climate model for the ice ages.
tldr: Introduces a modular framework to identify piecewise-smooth dynamical systems from trajectory data using geometry-constrained neural networks, addressing discontinuous dynamics.
motivation: Most data-driven system identification methods assume smooth dynamics, yet many real-world systems (e.g., friction, climate) exhibit discontinuities that are underexplored.
method: The framework estimates switching hyperplanes from data and learns smooth dynamics within each region via geometry-constrained neural networks; a novel architecture with a prescribed discontinuity set is introduced with approximation guarantees.
result: Validated on dry-friction oscillators and the PP04 climate model, showing accurate recovery of governing equations and detection of sliding motion.
conclusion: This work advances system identification for piecewise-smooth dynamics, filling a gap in the ML and applied mathematics literature.

title: A Fixed-Penalty Linearized Augmented Lagrangian Method With Classical Multiplier Updates
authors: Benqi Liu, Kangkang Deng, Zichen Wang, Zaiwen Wen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Augmented Lagrangian methods are effective for nonlinear equality-constrained optimization, but solving their nonlinear primal subproblems can be expensive. For smooth nonconvex problems with deterministic or stochastic objectives, we propose a nonlinear-residual linearized augmented Lagrangian method (NR-LALM) that replaces this subproblem by a regularized Gauss-Newton-type step while retaining the classical multiplier update based on the nonlinear constraint residual. The resulting step is computed from one symmetric positive-definite linear system, but the mismatch between the linearized primal model and the nonlinear-residual update produces a quadratic constraint-linearization error in the multiplier identity. We show that this error can be controlled under local regularity; multiplier boundedness and trajectory localization are derived rather than assumed. With fixed, accuracy-independent parameters, deterministic NR-LALM finds an [MATH]-approximate Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) pair in [MATH] iterations and first-order oracle evaluations. For stochastic objectives, a projected stochastic path-integrated differential estimator with safeguarded restarts requires, in expectation, [MATH] stochastic-gradient evaluations and [MATH] constraint and Jacobian evaluations. Compactness and a Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz condition further yield finite-length convergence of the deterministic primal-dual sequence. An optional minimum-norm second-order correction reduces the constraint-linearization error from second to fourth order without changing the complexity orders. All theoretical results are formalized in Lean 4. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted error orders and show favorable performance on high-dimensional deterministic and stochastic problems.
tldr: This paper proposes a novel linearized augmented Lagrangian method for nonlinear equality-constrained optimization with classical multiplier updates, providing rigorous complexity guarantees and formal verification in Lean 4.
motivation: The authors aim to reduce the computational cost of solving nonlinear primal subproblems in augmented Lagrangian methods, particularly for high-dimensional deterministic and stochastic optimization problems.
method: The method replaces the primal subproblem with a regularized Gauss-Newton-type step while retaining classical multiplier updates based on nonlinear residuals, and includes an optional minimum-norm second-order correction to reduce linearization error.
result: The deterministic algorithm achieves an approximate KKT point in O(epsilon^{-2}) iterations and oracle evaluations; the stochastic variant requires O(epsilon^{-4}) stochastic-gradient evaluations in expectation. All theoretical results are formalized in Lean 4.
conclusion: Numerical experiments confirm the predicted error orders and show competitive performance, making the method promising for large-scale optimization, though the topic is outside the scope of quantum information and related fields.

title: Sub-optimality Of Marton's Inner Bound For The Two-Receiver Broadcast Channel
authors: Mian Huang, Yanxiao Liu, Yi Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Marton's inner bound, the best-known achievable region for a general discrete memoryless broadcast channel, was proposed by Katalin Marton in 1979, and whether it always achieves the capacity region has remained open since then. In this paper, we establish its strict sub-optimality: we show that the capacity region of some discrete memoryless broadcast channels can be strictly larger than Marton's inner bound.
tldr: This paper proves that Marton's inner bound is strictly sub-optimal for two-receiver discrete memoryless broadcast channels, showing the capacity region can be larger than this long-standing bound.
motivation: Marton's inner bound, proposed in 1979, has been the best-known achievable region for broadcast channels, but its optimality remained open; this paper resolves the question by demonstrating its sub-optimality.
method: The authors construct specific discrete memoryless broadcast channels and provide an information-theoretic proof that the capacity region strictly contains Marton's inner bound.
result: They establish that there exist channels whose capacity region is strictly larger than Marton's inner bound, thus settling the open problem.
conclusion: This result implies that Marton's inner bound is not always tight, so new achievable regions are needed for broadcast channels.

title: String Rewriting Systems: Brief Introduction And Sample Of Open Problems
authors: Assaf Kfoury
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This document is the result of pulling together small parts of different lecture notes I have written over several decades for first-year graduate-level courses -- typically with the title Formal Methods -- which included many other topics of mathematical logic and theoretical computer science. After combining these materials, I updated the references and adjusted the text to account for progress accomplished in the intervening years.
