conclusion: The paper serves as an educational reference for graduate students, offering a starting point for research in string rewriting systems.

title: Enhancing Privacy In Federated Learning Via Dual Obfuscation Of Gradients And Training Images
authors: Yuki Itabashi, Hiroto Sawada, Mare Hirose, Shoko Imaizumi, Hitoshi Kiya
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training while keeping data locally at each client; however, recent studies have shown that training data can be reconstructed from shared model updates. To address this issue, this paper proposes a dual obfuscation method that enhances robustness against image restoration attacks by jointly obfuscating updated information and training images. The proposed method combines a robustness enhancement technique based on random binary weights, which randomly sets a portion of gradient elements to zero, with an image encryption technique. These techniques provide complementary protection by reducing the amount of original gradient information available to an attacker and the visual interpretability of reconstructed images, respectively. Furthermore, the image encryption technique allows independent keys to be used for each client and each image, avoiding explicit key sharing. Experimental results on an image classification task using a Vision Transformer (ViT) show that the proposed method reduces the visual information recovered by Attention Privacy Leakage (APRIL) under the evaluated settings without causing additional degradation in classification performance beyond that caused by image encryption. Although the proposed combination does not provide an absolute security guarantee, the results demonstrate the potential benefit of combining gradient modification and image encryption for privacy-enhanced federated learning.
tldr: This paper proposes a dual obfuscation method for federated learning, combining random gradient masking with image encryption to mitigate gradient inversion attacks.
motivation: Federated learning is vulnerable to gradient inversion attacks that reconstruct training images; the goal is to enhance privacy without sacrificing classification performance.
method: The method jointly applies a random binary weight technique that zeros out a fraction of gradient elements and an image encryption scheme with per-client, per-image independent keys, providing complementary protection.
result: Experiments on a Vision Transformer (ViT) image classification task show reduced visual information leakage from the APRIL attack compared to baseline, with no additional performance degradation beyond that from image encryption.
conclusion: The combination of gradient obfuscation and image encryption offers a potential privacy enhancement for federated learning, though it does not guarantee absolute security.

title: Copa: Continual Preference Optimization For Adaptive Prompt Injection Defense
authors: Roshan Sood, Onat Gungor, Tajana Rosing
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs remain vulnerable to prompt injection attacks, where adversarial instructions embedded in user inputs or external content manipulate model behavior and bypass safeguards. Existing defenses are predominantly static, relying on fixed alignment objectives or attack-specific filtering mechanisms that require redesign as new attack strategies emerge. While recent lifelong alignment methods address shifting user preferences, they do not account for adaptive adversaries that continually evolve to exploit weaknesses in previously learned defenses. This limitation is particularly important in real-world deployments, where evolving attack distributions necessitate continual adaptation without sacrificing robustness to previously encountered threats. We present COPA, a continual preference optimization framework that treats prompt-injection defense as a lifelong learning problem. Instead of one-time alignment, COPA incrementally incorporates feedback from newly observed attacks via GRPO-based optimization and uses margin-weighted experience replay to retain defenses against prior attack classes. This enables continuous adaptation to emerging threats while mitigating catastrophic forgetting and preserving general-purpose model capabilities. Across lifelong prompt injection attack streams, COPA reduces attack success rate by up to 6.3x and 4.4x on average compared to state-of-the-art defenses. These results highlight continual preference optimization as an effective paradigm for defending LLMs against adaptive adversaries.
tldr: COPA is a continual preference optimization framework that defends LLMs against evolving prompt injection attacks.
motivation: Static defenses fail to adapt to adaptive adversaries, and existing lifelong alignment methods do not account for continually evolving attack distributions.
method: COPA incrementally incorporates feedback from new attacks via GRPO-based optimization and uses margin-weighted experience replay to retain defenses against prior attack classes.
result: COPA reduces attack success rate by up to 6.3x and 4.4x on average compared to state-of-the-art defenses across lifelong attack streams.
conclusion: Continual preference optimization proves effective for defending LLMs against adaptive adversaries, highlighting a new paradigm for prompt injection defense.

title: Trustworthy Mobile Edge Caching: A Blockchain Approach To Mitigate Malicious Nodes And Incentivize Cache Sharing
authors: Motahare Ebrahimi, Nastooh Taheri Javan, Seyedakbar Mostafavi, Fatemeh Pakzaban
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As mobile network traffic continues to grow, content caching on edge servers is critical for reducing latency. However, challenges such as malicious edge servers that may delete or manipulate cached content, along with the limited capacity of these servers, need to be addressed. To overcome the capacity limitations, helper mobile nodes can contribute their cache resources. However, due to their selfish behavior, an incentive mechanism is necessary to encourage resource sharing. Additionally, these helper nodes can also be malicious. This paper proposes a blockchain-based trust management mechanism that addresses these challenges by accurately identifying trustworthy edge servers and mobile nodes. The proposed mechanism calculates both direct and indirect trust using smart contracts, ensuring that malicious nodes are effectively filtered out. Trustworthiness is determined based on mobile node satisfaction with the quality of service, and trust data is securely stored on the blockchain. To combat node selfishness, a reward mechanism is introduced to incentivize cache sharing. Furthermore, a blockchain-based authentication mechanism protects against node impersonation. Our approach optimizes trust, cache capacity, and cost efficiency while considering mobile node mobility, energy consumption, and computational power constraints during the consensus process. Simulation results show that the proposed method can accurately distinguish between honest and malicious servers, even with a 10% noise in data.
tldr: The paper proposes a blockchain-based trust management and incentive mechanism for mobile edge caching to mitigate malicious nodes and encourage cache sharing.
motivation: Mobile edge caching suffers from malicious edge servers and selfish helper nodes that may not share resources, requiring a trust and incentive framework.
method: The method uses smart contracts to compute direct and indirect trust, implement a reward mechanism for cache sharing, and provide blockchain-based authentication to prevent impersonation.
result: Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method accurately distinguishes honest from malicious servers even with 10% data noise.
conclusion: The blockchain-based approach effectively addresses trust and incentive problems in mobile edge caching, improving cache capacity and cost efficiency.

title: The Generalized Random Access Problem For Linear Codes
authors: Anina Gruica, Antonio Petrillo, Ferdinando Zullo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Random access is a central requirement in DNA-based storage systems: one would like to recover selected information symbols without sequencing the whole encoded object. A recent combinatorial model associates to a generator matrix [MATH] the random variable [MATH], measuring the number of sampled columns needed to recover the information vector [MATH]. We study the cardinality-based extremal and finite-geometric aspects of simultaneous multi-symbol recovery. For a nonempty set [MATH], let [MATH] denote the number of random column samples needed until all vectors [MATH], [MATH], lie in the span of the observed columns. This variable interpolates between the singleton random access problem and the full-recovery problem underlying coverage depth. For each [MATH], we introduce uniform worst-case and average parameters over all requested sets [MATH] with [MATH]. Using the known subset-counting formula for [MATH], we establish general upper and lower bounds for these parameters. In particular, the lower bounds are expressed through order statistics of the singleton recovery variables and specialize to the known singleton bounds when [MATH]. For systematic MDS encoders, we record an equivalent form of the known multi-symbol expectation formula and derive monotonicity and asymptotic consequences. For simplex encoders in arbitrary dimension, we obtain closed formulae in terms of Gaussian binomial coefficients; the full-recovery endpoint agrees with the known coverage-depth formula for simplex codes. Finally, in dimension three we study balanced quasi-arcs and compare their values with the simplex and MDS benchmarks.
tldr: This paper studies the combinatorial and finite-geometric aspects of the generalized random access problem for linear codes, focusing on multi-symbol recovery in DNA-based storage systems.
motivation: DNA-based storage requires efficient random access to specific information symbols without sequencing the entire encoded object, motivating a mathematical model for recovery efficiency.
method: The authors introduce random variables for the number of sampled columns needed to recover a set of information symbols, derive uniform worst-case and average parameters over requested sets, and analyze them using subset-counting formulas, order statistics, and finite geometry.
result: They establish general upper and lower bounds, obtain closed formulae for simplex encoders in arbitrary dimension, and study balanced quasi-arcs in dimension three, comparing them with simplex and MDS benchmarks.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive combinatorial analysis of the multi-symbol random access problem, extending known singleton recovery results and offering new tools for evaluating code performance in DNA storage.

title: Probabilities Beyond Belnap-Dunn Logic: Dealing With Gaps, Gluts And Reliability
authors: Ver\'onica Borja Macias, Marcelo E. Coniglio, Alejandro Hern\'andez-Tello
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the study of probability functions based on the 6-valued paradefinite (i.e., paraconsistent and paracomplete) logic LETK+. This logic is a powerful and versatile Logic of Evidence and Truth (LET) which is a conservative expansion of both classical logic and FDE. The framework introduced here allowed us to consider gaps, gluts, and reliability (or classicality) of the events, extending the detailed proposal for FDE-based probabilities presented by Klein, Majer, and Rafiee Rad. A distinctive feature of our proposal is the use of twist structure semantics, which gives rise to a natural interpretation of logical probabilities over LETK+ in terms of the three or six regions associated with each formula by a valuation in such models. The LETK+-probability functions are defined axiomatically and semantically, obtaining soundness and completeness results, as one would expect. Finally, conditional probabilities based on LETK+ are also studied. Specifically, both a semantic and a syntactic characterization of Jeffrey's update over LETK+-based probabilities is proposed, showing their equivalence.
tldr: The paper introduces a framework for probability functions based on the 6-valued paradefinite logic LETK+, handling gaps, gluts, and reliability via twist structure semantics.
motivation: To extend probability theory to non-classical logics that accommodate incomplete and inconsistent information, building on prior work with FDE-based probabilities.
method: Defines LETK+ with twist semantics, axiomatizes probability functions, proves soundness/completeness, and studies conditional probabilities via Jeffrey's update with semantic and syntactic characterizations.
result: Provides a rigorous probabilistic framework for LETK+ with soundness and completeness, and demonstrates equivalence of semantic and syntactic approaches to conditional probability updates.
conclusion: The work generalizes probability to paradefinite logics, enabling probabilistic reasoning about unreliable or contradictory evidence.

title: The Honeycomb Framework For Code Bounds
authors: William Gay, Fernando Granha Jeronimo, Lenny Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the honeycomb hierarchy, a representation-theoretic framework that gives new asymptotic upper bounds on [MATH]. Its first level is the two-row hyperoctahedral representation graph associated with type [MATH]. Retaining every two-row irreducible and every coordinate box-transfer channel, together with a moving-projection theorem, yields an explicit four-parameter exponent [MATH]. The earlier whole-cube exponent [MATH] is a boundary restriction of this optimization, whereas the fully optimized second MRRW exponent [MATH] is an exact symmetric slice. The prior best curve is the combined [MATH], which uses a constant-weight branch [MATH]. Replacing only the whole-cube branch by the honeycomb bound gives [MATH]. We prove, on [MATH], \[ R_2(\delta)\le \kappa_{}(\delta) \le \kappa_{}(\delta) \le R_{}(\delta)<R_{}(\delta), \qquad \kappa_H(\delta)=R_{}(\delta). \] The hierarchy has two further directions. Increasing the representation depth replaces scalar by matrix-valued transfers on the hive. Increasing the anchor depth localizes it in a stable-set hierarchy. The resulting bounds are monotone in both directions and eventually recover [MATH]. A complementary Horn--channel hierarchy gives matrix optimizations whose [MATH] level is [MATH] and whose [MATH] level is a stronger bound. Already at low levels, they can be used to improve the strongest previous general bounds, while the honeycomb framework provides a route towards tighter bounds.
tldr: Introduces a representation-theoretic honeycomb framework yielding new asymptotic upper bounds on code rates, improving upon the MRRW bound.
motivation: To tighten the best-known upper bounds for classical error-correcting codes, which have remained largely static despite advances in the field.
method: Constructs a honeycomb hierarchy based on the hyperoctahedral group's two-row irreducible representations, combined with a moving-projection theorem and coordinate box-transfer channels, to formulate a four-parameter optimization for the exponent.
result: Proves that the honeycomb bound strictly improves the whole-cube branch and matches the second MRRW exponent on a symmetric slice, yielding tighter curves than previous general bounds.
conclusion: The honeycomb framework provides a scalable path for deriving progressively tighter code bounds through increased representation and anchor depths, potentially unifying and surpassing prior techniques.

title: Linguistic Holonomy And Statistical Watermarks: Inner Geometry Of Meaning-Preserving Transformations
authors: Daniele Corradetti
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19369v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Statistical watermarks for language models live in the freedom of the signifier: they choose among tokens that are nearly equivalent in meaning, and they are therefore eroded by exactly those transformations which move the form of a text while leaving its content in place. The literature measures such transformations by their endpoint, through the semantic similarity between the original and the rewritten text. We show that the endpoint is the wrong statistic. Adapting the formalism of linguistic loops, we prove that the invariant of a chain of meaning-preserving transformations factorises canonically into an endpoint part and a holonomy in the stabiliser of the initial state, the second of which the semantic deficit cannot see; the loop rotation is parallel transport on the unit sphere of the embedding space, so that the analogy with the Wilson loop becomes a theorem rather than a figure of speech. On the side of the detector we prove an exact identity: the residual statistic is proportional to the number of positions whose seeding window survived intact, from which the decay law [MATH] follows as the independent-edit corollary. The identity has a disconcerting consequence, which we confirm to three decimal places: at one and the same retention rate the surviving signal may be one half of the original, one quarter of it, or exactly nothing, according only to where the edits fall.
tldr: This paper presents a geometric framework for meaning-preserving transformations in language models, showing that the invariant factorizes into endpoint and holonomy, and derives a decay law for statistical watermarks.
motivation: Statistical watermarks are eroded by meaning-preserving transformations, but current measures only consider endpoint semantic similarity, which is inadequate.
method: The authors adapt linguistic loops formalism and prove that the invariant factorizes canonically, interpreting loop rotation as parallel transport on the unit sphere of embedding space, analogous to Wilson loops.
result: They prove an exact identity for the residual statistic and derive a decay law, showing that the surviving signal can vary dramatically (half, quarter, or nothing) depending on edit positions, confirmed numerically.
conclusion: The endpoint is the wrong statistic; the holonomy in the stabilizer is essential for understanding watermark robustness against meaning-preserving edits.

title: Constant-round Quantum Advantage In Communication Complexity For Total Functions
authors: Fran\c{c}ois Le Gall Atsuya Hasegawa
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19787v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that there exists a total function for which there is a polynomial gap between the randomized and the constant-round quantum communication complexity. Previously, such a separation was known only for quantum protocols using polynomially many rounds.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that constant-round quantum communication protocols can achieve a polynomial advantage over randomized classical protocols for a total function, extending previous results that required polynomially many rounds.
motivation: The work aims to investigate whether quantum communication advantages persist even with a limited number of rounds, which was open for constant-round protocols.
method: The authors construct a total function and use information-theoretic techniques to prove a polynomial separation between randomized and constant-round quantum communication complexity.
result: They exhibit a total function where constant-round quantum communication complexity is polynomially smaller than randomized communication complexity, a separation previously known only for protocols with polynomially many rounds.
conclusion: The result establishes that constant-round quantum protocols can offer significant communication savings over classical randomized protocols, emphasizing the power of quantum communication even with limited interaction.

title: RMWorld: Task-Aware Radio World Models With Value-of-Information Guided Multi-Trial Learning For Multi-UAV Communication Control
authors: Xiucheng Wang, Nan Cheng, Junxi Huan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable multi-UAV communication control depends on predicting which aerial links will serve traffic before measurements are available. Radio world models (radio WMs) make such planning tractable, but their errors are nonuniform: a globally accurate model may still fail along high-demand corridors or association boundaries where rate errors reverse control decisions. This mismatch creates a learning challenge. Link queries must reduce decision-relevant channel uncertainty, while counterfactual trials must be filtered so that biased rollouts do not corrupt the policy. Existing acquisition and model-based control treat these budgets separately, valuing uncertainty, coverage, or optimistic return rather than risk reduction. We present RMWorld, a task-aware radio-WM framework that couples value-of-information channel calibration with credibility-diversity multi-trial selection. A biased propagation formula is corrected by a Bayesian residual, and each link is valued by its exact one-label reduction in locally linearized task-integrated posterior rate variance. Counterfactual branches are selected by a task-gated log-determinant objective, followed by conflict projection and fixed-batch validation. We derive the variance-reduction identity, prove posterior task-risk equivalence and the submodular greedy guarantee, and establish a scoped first-order non-interference result. Across 100 paired 3GPP trials RMWorld reaches 0.949~bit/s/Hz task-weighted RMSE, and across 30 severe-load DeepMIMO trials it reduces median backlog by 0.967 versus Ensemble UCB at 37.5\% more offline rollouts.
tldr: This paper proposes a task-aware radio world model framework for multi-UAV communication control, focusing on uncertainty reduction and multi-trial learning, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper addresses the challenge of predicting aerial link quality for reliable multi-UAV communication, where existing models suffer from nonuniform errors and fail to reduce decision-relevant uncertainty.
method: RMWorld couples value-of-information channel calibration with credibility-diversity multi-trial selection, using a Bayesian residual correction and a submodular greedy objective for counterfactual branch selection.
result: The framework achieves 0.949 bit/s/Hz task-weighted RMSE across 100 3GPP trials and reduces median backlog by 0.967 versus Ensemble UCB in DeepMIMO trials.
conclusion: The proposed method demonstrates significant improvements in task-aware radio world modeling, but it is entirely outside the scope of quantum information science.

title: Rural Commute Patterns
authors: Mohamed Khalafalla, Doreen Kobelo, Thobias Sando, Janeroza Matyeni
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transportation provides access to employment opportunities and essential services such as healthcare services, while urban areas have various transportation options, the situation differs in rural areas. Rural residents often have longer commute distances, limited access to public transit, and extended waiting times for public transportation if they exist, which can significantly impact their access to vital services and job opportunities. This study used data from the 2017 NHTS survey to examine the commuting patterns in rural areas by utilizing multinomial logistic regression to determine how various factors impact the choice of mode of transport in rural areas. Findings from this study revealed a higher dependency, 92.1%, on using personal vehicles when making trips in rural areas. Multinomial logistic regression results showed that socio-demographics, household, and trip characteristics affect the mode of transport used in a trip. Older adults, females, and individuals with higher education levels than high school graduates are less likely to use public transit when making trips. For household characteristics, the availability of vehicles in a household and households with higher income levels have lower probabilities of making a trip using public transit. Longer trip distances reduce the likelihood of a trip using active commuting modes such as walking and biking. These findings provide insights into understanding the transportation behaviors in rural areas and provide knowledge to be used in the planning and developing of transportation projects to promote equitable and accessible transportation in rural areas.
tldr: This paper analyzes rural commuting patterns using NHTS data, finding heavy reliance on personal vehicles and factors influencing mode choice via multinomial logistic regression.
motivation: Rural residents face longer commutes and limited transit options, affecting access to jobs and services. Understanding these patterns can inform equitable transportation planning.
method: Used 2017 NHTS survey data and multinomial logistic regression to model mode choice as a function of socio-demographics, household, and trip characteristics.
result: Found 92.1% dependency on personal vehicles; older adults, females, higher education, vehicle availability, higher income, and longer trips reduce public transit or active commuting use.
conclusion: These insights can guide transportation projects to improve accessibility and equity in rural areas.

title: Second-Order Continuum Model For Disordered Traffic
authors: Shashank Rajput, Venkatesan Kanagaraj, Martin Treiber, Gowri Asaithambi, Ostap Okhrin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, a two-dimensional second-order macroscopic traffic flow model is proposed to capture the complex dynamics of disordered traffic by explicitly incorporating coupled longitudinal and lateral interactions. The framework extends the classical continuity equation to two spatial dimensions and introduces acceleration equations consisting of self-driven, interaction-induced, and road-boundary-related components. The macroscopic longitudinal acceleration is formulated based on the Full Velocity Difference Model (FVDM), while lateral dynamics are governed by interaction principles consistent with the Optimal Velocity Model (OVM). The explicit inclusion of road-boundary effects enables the representation of vehicle confinement and space-sharing behavior that are essential in lane-free and weakly lane-disciplined traffic systems. The model is examined through a series of numerical experiments in which longitudinal and lateral dynamics are analysed individually as well as simultaneously within a coupled two-dimensional setting under a range of initial conditions, including transitions between free-flow, medium congestion, and heavy congestion, and different lateral density configurations. The simulations demonstrate the model's ability to reproduce key traffic features such as shockwave propagation, lateral dispersion, vehicle rearrangement, and stable density evolution across the road width. The numerical scheme, based on upwind and Lax-Friedrichs discretisations, ensures stable solutions of the coupled partial differential equations. Overall, the proposed framework provides a robust macroscopic description of disordered traffic and offers a consistent basis for analysing two-dimensional vehicular flow dynamics.
tldr: This paper proposes a two-dimensional second-order macroscopic traffic flow model for disordered traffic, incorporating coupled longitudinal and lateral interactions.
motivation: To capture the complex dynamics of disordered traffic where lane discipline is weak, requiring explicit modeling of coupled longitudinal and lateral interactions.
method: Extends the classical continuity equation to two spatial dimensions with acceleration equations for self-driven, interaction-induced, and road-boundary components, based on FVDM and OVM, solved using upwind and Lax-Friedrichs discretizations.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate the model's ability to reproduce shockwave propagation, lateral dispersion, vehicle rearrangement, and stable density evolution across the road width.
conclusion: The framework provides a robust macroscopic description of two-dimensional vehicular flow dynamics in disordered traffic conditions.

title: Geometry-Encoded Multireceiver Fluorometry Enables Full-Range Nonlinear Quantification Under The Inner Filter Effect
authors: Shuiyi Tan, Nai-Quan Zhu, Olivier J. F. Martin, Yuchao Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The inner filter effect (IFE) transforms the nominally linear fluorescence-concentration relationship into a geometry-dependent and often nonmonotonic response, resulting in reduced sensitivity, concentration ambiguity, and inaccurate underestimation at high optical densities. Here, we introduce a spatially encoded multireceiver fluorometric strategy that does not eliminate or correct the IFE, but instead harnesses the spatial fluorescence attenuation induced by IFE as an additional quantitative encoding dimension. Fluorescence generated along the excitation axis is integrated over independently positioned receiver windows, and concentration is recovered by nonlinear optimization of the joint fluorescent intensity vector. Tryptophan was selected as a biomedically relevant model fluorophore to validate the proposed strategy. Single-window calibration exhibited vanishing-gradient boundary and two-valued concentration inversions, whereas two spatially separated receiver windows restored global identifiability across the full concentration range. Screening of 35 two-receiver geometries identified the minimum-uncertainty configuration, achieving an average 95% error half-width of mean E_95= 0.884 mg/L, and the maximum-sensitivity configuration, reaching a noise-normalized response sensitivity of mean S_N=3.832 a.u./(mg/L). By converting spatial attenuation into a multidimensional concentration coordinate, this approach extends quantitative fluorescence analysis without dilution, a separate absorbance measurement, or piecewise calibration and provides a general metrology framework for fluorescence metrology even under strong IFE conditions.
tldr: This paper introduces a spatially encoded multireceiver fluorometric strategy that harnesses the inner filter effect to enable full-range nonlinear quantification without dilution or correction.
motivation: The inner filter effect causes nonlinear and nonmonotonic relationships in fluorescence concentration measurements, leading to reduced sensitivity and concentration ambiguity. Existing methods require dilution or correction; the authors aim to exploit the effect instead.
method: Fluorescence along the excitation axis is integrated over multiple receiver windows at different positions, and concentration is recovered via nonlinear optimization of the joint intensity vector. Tryptophan was used as a model and 35 geometries were screened.
result: Two spatially separated receiver windows restored global identifiability. They found configurations for minimum uncertainty and maximum sensitivity, achieving an average 95% error half-width of 0.884 mg/L and a noise-normalized sensitivity of 3.832 a.u./(mg/L).
conclusion: This approach provides a general metrology framework for fluorescence quantification even under strong inner filter effect, without dilution or extra measurements.

title: Shift Or Curtail? How Much Data-center Flexibility Is Worth Depends On The Host Power Grid
authors: Saroj Khanal, Geon Roh, Boyu Yao, Abraham Silverman, Dennice Gayme, Charalambos Konstantinou, Jip Kim, Yury Dvorkin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data-center growth risks overbuilding power grid infrastructure and stranding capital. Flexible data-center operation can defer infrastructure investments, but its value depends on the flexibility mechanism and the host power grid characteristics. We classify data-center load as firm, flexible or interruptible, and embed them in capacity expansion applied to market-organized, fossil-heavy PJM and carbon-capped, centrally coordinated Korea. In PJM, the flexibility value is spatial: shifting workloads between zones reduces system cost by 6% in 2028 and 19% in 2038, avoiding 4.4 GW and 8.9 GW of gas and nuclear generation. In Korea, it is temporal: shifting load into midday solar hours makes 0.5 GW of additional solar worth building in 2028 and avoids 1.2 GW of gas and 0.3 GW of batteries in 2038. In both, realistic event-shape limits diminish the value of curtailment. The results show that flexibility procurement and its value are driven by grid characteristics and policy objectives.
tldr: This paper analyzes the value of data-center flexibility in deferring power grid infrastructure investments, showing that the optimal flexibility mechanism depends on grid characteristics and policy goals.
motivation: Data-center growth risks overbuilding power grid infrastructure and stranding capital; flexible operation can defer investments, but its value depends on the flexibility mechanism and host power grid.
method: The authors classify data-center load as firm, flexible, or interruptible and embed them in capacity expansion models, applied to the PJM market and the Korean carbon-capped grid.
result: In PJM, flexibility is spatially valuable, reducing system cost by 6% and 19% in 2028 and 2038, avoiding gas and nuclear generation; in Korea, temporal flexibility enables more solar adoption and avoids gas and batteries, though realistic event-shape limits reduce curtailment value.
conclusion: Flexibility procurement and its value are driven by grid characteristics and policy objectives, not a one-size-fits-all approach.

title: Microlocal Analysis Of Non-linear Artifacts In Cone Beam Ct
authors: Alexander Katsevich James W. Webber
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a novel microlocal analysis of beam hardening artifacts arising in cone-beam X-ray CT, where the set of X-ray sources is restricted to a 1D smooth curve [MATH]. We show that, when the CT data is modeled in the standard way using the Beer Lambert law, the exponential term in the model creates singularities in the data that are not present in the linear X-ray transform. We assume that the attenuation coefficient [MATH] (the reconstruction target) has a jump discontinuity across a surface [MATH], and is smooth otherwise. We prove that these additional singularities in the data occur when the X-ray beam is tangent to [MATH] at two points simultaneously. To investigate how the singularities in the data propagate to the reconstruction space, we apply Filtered Back Projection (FBP) type reconstruction. We prove that the artifacts due to beam hardening are locally of conormal type, and lie on a 2-D surface which is the union of all double tangent rays which intersect [MATH]. The artifacts are notably weaker than the reconstructed jumps of [MATH] (i.e., the desired singularities), and we quantify this using the order of the corresponding conormal distributions. While our primary theory applies to the regions of [MATH] that are smooth, we also extend our theory to non-smooth [MATH] with "ridges." These arise where [MATH] is locally the intersection of two smooth surface patches meeting transversely along a curve (e.g., the edge of a cuboid). In addition, we present simulated reconstructions of metal objects in circular cone-beam CT to validate our theory.
tldr: A microlocal analysis characterizes beam hardening artifacts in cone-beam CT as conormal distributions on surfaces generated by double tangent rays, showing they are weaker than true edge singularities.
motivation: To understand and mathematically characterize beam hardening artifacts in CT imaging, which arise from non-linear effects in the Beer-Lambert law.
method: Uses microlocal analysis to study singularities introduced by the exponential term in CT data, and analyzes their propagation through filtered back projection.
result: Proves that beam hardening artifacts are conormal distributions on 2D surfaces, and are weaker than the desired reconstruction singularities, with extensions to non-smooth surfaces.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical framework for understanding beam hardening artifacts, validated by simulations.

title: From The Half-Order Recurrence To General Fractional-Order Differentiation On Monomials: Functional Continuation And Operator Composition
authors: Davit Kapanadze
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work develops a general-order fractional differentiation operator on monomials from the discrete half-order coefficient structure established in Part I. Starting from the one-step transfer law of the integer coefficient family, the discrete coefficient relation is continued to a real argument and a canonical Gamma-functional form is selected under the stated normalization and regularity requirements. The operator order is then extended beyond one half by dividing the first derivative into equal operator steps, leading from orders 1/m and k/m to general rational and real orders. The resulting coefficient is independently verified through the addition law for operator orders on the monomial system, subject to the requirement that all intermediate expressions in the composition are defined. On the corresponding parameter domain, the construction yields the standard Gamma-ratio monomial formula for fractional differentiation. For nonnegative integer orders it reduces to ordinary repeated differentiation, while for positive non-integer orders it agrees at the monomial level with the left-sided Riemann-Liouville formula with lower limit 0. Its relation to the Caputo operator is also discussed, including the distinction for constants and low-degree polynomial terms. The aim is not to introduce a new classical fractional derivative, but to provide a constructive algebraic-operator route from a discrete coefficient law to the general fractional-order monomial formula, clarifying the roles of functional continuation, Gamma normalization, and operator composition.
tldr: This paper constructs a fractional-order differentiation operator on monomials via functional continuation and operator composition, yielding the standard Gamma-ratio formula.
motivation: To provide a constructive algebraic-operator derivation of fractional differentiation from a discrete coefficient law, clarifying the roles of functional continuation and Gamma normalization.
method: The method involves continuing the discrete half-order coefficient relation to real orders, using Gamma function normalization, and extending to general orders via operator composition and addition law.
result: The construction yields the standard monomial fractional derivative formula, matches Riemann-Liouville for positive non-integer orders, and reduces to ordinary derivatives for integer orders.
conclusion: The paper offers a purely algebraic route to fractional differentiation, clarifying the underlying structure without introducing a new derivative definition.

title: Existence Of Periodic Solutions For Hamiltonian Inclusion Systems Using Clarke Duality
authors: Fernando D. Mazzone Stefania M. Demaria
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of periodic solutions for Hamiltonian differential inclusions under growth conditions involving a G-function.
tldr: This paper proves the existence of periodic solutions for Hamiltonian differential inclusions with growth conditions involving a G-function using Clarke duality.
motivation: To establish existence results for periodic solutions in nonsmooth Hamiltonian systems, which are relevant in nonlinear analysis and control theory.
method: The authors employ Clarke duality and growth conditions with a G-function to handle the multivalued nature of the inclusion.
result: The paper demonstrates the existence of periodic solutions under the stated growth conditions.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the theory of differential inclusions, but are unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A High-Order Rank-Adaptive Implicit Algorithm For Solving High Dimensional Diffusion Equations Using The Hierarchical Tucker Decomposition
authors: Paolo Bosques-Paulet
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a high-order rank-adaptive implicit integrator for the tensor solution of high-dimensional diffusion equations. We extend the 3D version of this method from the Tucker decomposition to higher dimensions using the hierarchical Tucker (HT) decomposition, since the storage complexity for the Tucker decomposition increases exponentially with the number of dimensions [MATH]. The HT format avoids this issue by decomposing the solution according to a binary tree consisting of bases for each dimension and core tensors which connect the bases. Spectral methods are considered for spatial discretization, and diagonally implicit Runge-Kutta methods are considered for time discretization. At each stage of the Runge-Kutta method, the bases computed at the previous stages are augmented to predict the upcoming basis and construct projection subspaces. By projecting onto these enriched subspaces, the bases and cores can be updated in a sequential manner going up the tree from leaf-to-root. Unlike the 3D Tucker method which has a single core tensor, the HT method also updates the intermediate core tensors. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the method observes high-order accuracy, and test how well the integrator captures the solution rank for various sets of time-dependent diffusion coefficients.
tldr: This paper presents a high-order rank-adaptive implicit integrator for solving high-dimensional diffusion equations using the hierarchical Tucker decomposition.
motivation: To efficiently solve high-dimensional diffusion equations by leveraging tensor decompositions to mitigate the curse of dimensionality.
method: Extends a 3D Tucker-based method to higher dimensions using hierarchical Tucker (HT) decomposition, employing spectral spatial discretization and diagonally implicit Runge-Kutta time stepping, with rank-adaptive basis and core updates along the HT tree.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy and effective rank capture for time-dependent diffusion coefficients.
conclusion: The proposed HT-based rank-adaptive integrator is a promising approach for high-dimensional diffusion problems.

title: Outer Contact Billiards
authors: Connor Jackman Ana Chavez Caliz
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce outer contact billiards as an odd dimensional counterpart to outer symplectic billiards. Until now, outer billiards have only been considered in even dimensional symplectic vector spaces. By projectivizing outer symplectic billiards, we obtain outer contact billiards, where the affine midpoint condition descends to its projective analog, namely harmonic conjugation. We prove that outer contact billiards generate contactomorphisms. For quadratic surfaces in [MATH], we show that the correspondence is completely integrable: its domain is foliated by invariant quadrics and, on each leaf, the dynamics is determined by the iteration of an explicit linear transformation. We also establish two rigidity results for periodic trajectories: outer contact billiards admit no 3-periodic orbits and, among quadratic tables, only one admits 4-periodic orbits.
tldr: Introduces outer contact billiards as an odd-dimensional analog of outer symplectic billiards and analyzes their dynamical properties.
motivation: Extends outer billiards to contact geometry, which has not been previously explored.
method: Uses projectivization to define outer contact billiards, with harmonic conjugation as the projective analog of the midpoint condition, and proves they generate contactomorphisms.
result: Shows complete integrability for quadratic surfaces via invariant quadrics and explicit linear transformations, and establishes rigidity results: no 3-periodic orbits and only one quadratic table admits 4-periodic orbits.
conclusion: Provides a new class of billiards in contact geometry with rich dynamics and rigidity, contributing to the study of integrable systems and periodic orbit theory.

title: A Rock-paper-scissors Mandelbrot Set
authors: Charlotte Aten
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The titular object of this paper is an analogue of the Mandelbrot set over the 3-dimensional real algebra whose multiplication is the bilinear extension of the rock-paper-scissors operation. In order to study the dynamics of the mappings [MATH] in this setting, a notion of holomorphy for functions on general finite-dimensional real algebras is introduced. Under a mild assumption it is shown that for such algebras holomorphy is always equivalent to solving a finite system of linear first-order PDEs generalizing the Cauchy-Riemann equations. Code is provided for generating animations of these fractals and for exploring them in a video game format.
tldr: 该论文在三维实代数中推广了Mandelbrot集，引入了一种全纯性概念，并提供了生成分形和探索视频游戏的代码。
motivation: 研究石头剪刀布操作定义的代数中的迭代动力学。
method: 引入有限维实代数上的全纯性，将其等价于广义Cauchy-Riemann方程组。
result: 证明了在某些假设下，全纯性等价于线性PDE系统，并提供了代码。
conclusion: 该论文是数学分形分析，与量子信息等领域无关。

title: Equidistribution And Thermodynamics At Infinity
authors: Godofredo Iommi, Felipe Riquelme, An\'ibal Velozo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove level-2 large deviation upper bounds for potentials on countable Markov shifts and for suspension semi-flows over countable Markov shifts. For strongly positive recurrent potentials, we establish equidistribution of weighted empirical measures toward the corresponding equilibrium state. We then apply these results to interval maps, obtaining, in particular, equidistribution and large-deviation estimates for measures supported on boundary points. For the Gauss map, this yields equidistribution results on rational numbers, including a theorem of David and Shapira.
tldr: The paper proves level-2 large deviation upper bounds and equidistribution results for countable Markov shifts and suspensions, with applications to interval maps including the Gauss map.
motivation: To extend thermodynamic formalism and equidistribution results to non-compact settings and countable state spaces.
method: Uses thermodynamic formalism, large deviation techniques, and analysis of potentials on countable Markov shifts and suspension semi-flows.
result: Establishes level-2 large deviation upper bounds and equidistribution of weighted empirical measures toward equilibrium states, with applications to boundary measures and rational numbers for the Gauss map.
conclusion: Provides new tools for equidistribution and large deviations in dynamical systems, but outside the scope of the specified research interests.

title: The Number Of Limit Cycles Of Piecewise Linear Li\'enard Systems
authors: Hebai Chen, Zhijie Li, Rui Zhang, Xiang Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the planar Li\'{e}nard differential system [MATH], [MATH], where [MATH] is a piecewise linear function, Tonnelier (SIAM J. Appl. Math., 2002) conjectured that the maximum number of limit cycles of the system is [MATH] when [MATH] has [MATH] fold points and no jump points, and [MATH] when [MATH] has [MATH] jump points and no fold points. This conjecture was confirmed by Llibre et al. (J. Nonlinear Sci., 2015) (resp. Chen et al. (J. London Math. Soc., 2026a)) when [MATH] has one fold point and no jump points (resp. two fold points). More recently, Chen et al. (J. London Math. Soc., 2026b) proved that the conjecture is correct when [MATH] has no fold points and one jump point. All other cases remain open. Here we verify that the lower bound for the maximum number of limit cycles of the system can be [MATH] when [MATH] has only [MATH] fold points, and [MATH] when [MATH] has only [MATH] jump points, thereby confirming the lower bound part of Tonnelier's conjecture. Moreover, when [MATH] has [MATH] jump points and [MATH] fold points, [MATH], we also show that the system can have [MATH] limit cycles. In addition, a complete classification of the {dynamics} near infinity for this class of systems is provided.
tldr: This paper confirms lower bounds on the maximum number of limit cycles in piecewise linear Liénard systems with fold and jump points, and provides a complete classification of dynamics near infinity.
motivation: The paper addresses Tonnelier's conjecture about the maximum number of limit cycles in piecewise linear Liénard systems, which has been open for several cases.
method: The authors use analytical techniques to construct systems with the conjectured number of limit cycles and analyze the dynamics near infinity.
result: They verify the lower bound for systems with fold points and jump points, and show that systems with both can have a certain number of limit cycles. They also classify the dynamics near infinity.
conclusion: The results confirm part of Tonnelier's conjecture and provide a fuller understanding of limit cycle bounds in these systems.

title: An Exact Structural Identity And Its Normal Form Consequences In A Modified Leslie--Gower Model
authors: Roberto Albarr\'an-Garc\'ia, Martha Alvarez-Ram\'irez, Marco Polo Garc\'ia-Rivera
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zhao and Zhao (2026) established a codimension-four Bogdanov--Takens singularity in a modified Leslie--Gower predator--prey model through a recursive normal form computation. We show that the nonlinear coefficients governing the restriction of the reduced system to the singularity's distinguished eigendirection are not independent. Instead, a single exact rational identity, already present in the transformed equations, generates the entire family of pure Taylor coefficients and proves that their simultaneous vanishing is an exact all orders property rather than a finite-order coincidence. We further show that this structural identity propagates through the planar Bogdanov--Takens normal form algorithm of Kuznetsov (2005). Although the pure coefficients vanish identically, the corresponding normal form coefficients are generated by mixed quadratic interactions. This leads to an explicit characterization of the degenerate Bogdanov--Takens locus and reduces the search for higher-order Bogdanov--Takens degeneracies to a single explicit algebraic condition.
tldr: The paper reveals an exact structural identity in a modified Leslie-Gower model that explains the vanishing of pure Taylor coefficients and characterizes the degenerate Bogdanov-Takens locus.
motivation: To understand the underlying structure of a codimension-four Bogdanov-Takens singularity and to simplify the search for higher-order degeneracies in the model.
method: The authors analyze the nonlinear coefficients in the reduced system, identify a rational identity that generates all pure Taylor coefficients, and propagate this identity through the planar Bogdanov-Takens normal form algorithm.
result: They prove that the pure coefficients vanish identically as an exact all-orders property, while normal form coefficients arise from mixed quadratic interactions, leading to an explicit algebraic condition for higher-order degeneracies.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper structural understanding of the singularity and reduces the search for higher-order Bogdanov-Takens degeneracies to a single explicit condition.

title: Evo-GTransNet For Parabolic PDEs: A Fixed-Feature Galerkin Method Of Lines With Quadrature-Mass Orthonormalization
authors: Jin Zhao Lili Ju
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop an evolutionary generalized transferable neural network (Evo-GTransNet) solver for parabolic partial differential equations, formulated as a retained-space fixed-feature Galerkin method of lines. A GTransNet provides the prescribed spatial dictionary, while only the retained output coefficients evolve, thereby avoiding nonlinear training during time integration. To address severe mass-matrix ill-conditioning, we apply a quadrature-weighted truncated singular value decomposition (SVD) to select the numerically resolved trial space, followed by a separate rescaling that makes its basis orthonormal with respect to the assembly-quadrature mass inner product. Rank truncation modifies the approximation space, whereas the subsequent orthonormalization changes only its coordinate representation and preserves the retained discrete functions in exact arithmetic. The resulting semidiscrete coefficient system has an identity mass matrix, and we establish a semidiscrete energy law for symmetric linear parabolic problems. With the implicit midpoint scheme for time discretization, we further prove the contractivity of the method and derive a conditional fully discrete error estimate in which the error is controlled by the retained-space approximation error and the consistency defects. Numerical experiments demonstrate second-order temporal convergence using repeated feature samples together with separate assembly and validation quadratures, and quantify the accuracy of the retained space in the presence of severe raw-mass ill-conditioning. For the high-frequency and multiscale benchmark problems considered here, GTransNet achieves the smallest mean validation errors among the tested fixed-feature dictionaries at the same nominal output dimension.
tldr: This paper introduces a neural network-based solver for parabolic PDEs using a fixed-feature Galerkin method of lines with quadrature-mass orthonormalization to handle ill-conditioning.
motivation: To develop an efficient and accurate neural network solver for parabolic PDEs, addressing the challenge of severe mass-matrix ill-conditioning while avoiding nonlinear training during time integration.
method: The method uses a GTransNet to provide a spatial dictionary, applies quadrature-weighted truncated SVD to select the resolved trial space, and orthonormalizes the basis with respect to the assembly-quadrature mass inner product. Time discretization uses the implicit midpoint scheme.
result: The paper proves a semidiscrete energy law, contractivity, and a conditional fully discrete error estimate. Numerical experiments demonstrate second-order temporal convergence and smallest mean validation errors compared to other fixed-feature dictionaries.
conclusion: The proposed approach effectively mitigates mass-matrix ill-conditioning, providing a reliable and accurate solver for parabolic PDEs with theoretical guarantees.

title: Open Cover Specification Property And Chaos
authors: Shweta Wadhwani, Devender Kumar, A R Prasannan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the open cover specification property and its role in the study of topological dynamical systems. We show that this property is a topological invariant and a natural extension of the classical topological specification property from uniform spaces to general topological spaces, and that it is preserved under infinite products with compositions. We further prove that on regular spaces, the strong open cover specification property implies Devaney chaos, and that on locally compact, first countable Hausdorff spaces, it guarantees both distributional chaos and Li Yorke chaos. These results demonstrate the significance of the open cover specification property in linking topological structure with dynamical complexity.
tldr: This paper studies the open cover specification property in topological dynamical systems, linking it to various notions of chaos.
motivation: To generalize the classical specification property to broader topological spaces and explore its implications for dynamical complexity.
method: The authors define the open cover specification property on general topological spaces, prove its invariance under topological conjugacy and infinite products, and analyze its consequences on regular and locally compact Hausdorff spaces.
result: They show the property is a topological invariant, extends the classic specification property, and implies Devaney chaos, distributional chaos, and Li-Yorke chaos under suitable conditions.
conclusion: The open cover specification property serves as a bridge between topological structure and dynamical complexity, but the work is purely mathematical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: High-Multiplicity Flexible Job Shops: From Exact Recurrent Fluid Attainment To Structure-Guided Finite-Horizon Scheduling
authors: Wenjun Zheng, Wei Qu, Weilin Cai, Jianfeng Mao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-multiplicity flexible job shops involve many copies of a small set of job types that must be scheduled on alternative machines. Fluid relaxations provide scalable workload lower bounds, but their fractional machine allocations do not define feasible schedules for individual jobs. We show that, after a suitable finite scaling, an optimal fluid allocation can be realized exactly by a feasible repeating discrete schedule. The construction scales the fluid allocation to integer operation counts, places the resulting operations in nonoverlapping machine intervals, repeats this arrangement, and links operations across repetitions into individual jobs without moving any interval, thereby enforcing job precedence while preserving machine feasibility. For growing finite instances with the same job-type composition, even with a fixed number of extra jobs, the gap between the optimal makespan and the fluid lower bound remains bounded by a constant; hence the relative gap vanishes as the instance grows. Guided by this repeated structure, we develop type-based cyclic template replay (TCTR), which searches job-type templates using an optimization model whose size does not grow with the number of job copies and replays the selected template on the full instance. On 676 multiplicity-expanded public flexible-job-shop instances, TCTR is feasible in every case and achieves a 1.54% mean gap to the fluid lower bound, compared with 5.32% for a job-indexed adaptive large-neighborhood search and 6.18% for a hybrid genetic algorithm.
tldr: This paper addresses high-multiplicity flexible job shop scheduling using fluid relaxations and cyclic templates, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to find feasible schedules for many copies of a small set of job types in flexible job shops, where fluid relaxations provide lower bounds but not feasible schedules.
method: The authors show that a scaled fluid allocation can be realized exactly by a repeating discrete schedule, and introduce a type-based cyclic template replay (TCTR) method that searches templates independent of the number of job copies.
result: On 676 public instances, TCTR achieves a 1.54% mean gap to the fluid lower bound, outperforming other methods, and the gap remains bounded by a constant for growing finite instances.
conclusion: The repeated structure enables efficient scheduling with a bounded gap, providing a practical approach for high-multiplicity job shops.

title: Dangling Points In Area-minimizing Meissner Polyhedra
authors: Beniamin Bogosel
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Meissner polyhedra are constant-width bodies obtained from extremal finite sets of unit diameter. Such a generating set may contain dangling points, namely points having exactly two diametric neighbors. This article studies whether these points can play an essential role in surface-area minimization. Given an extremal set we show that the smallest surface area among the Meissner polyhedra based on it cannot increase by deleting a dangling point. Adding a dangling point cannot decrease the smallest achievable surface area. This reduces the search for area-minimizing Meissner polyhedra to generating sets without dangling points.
tldr: This paper studies Meissner polyhedra, constant-width bodies derived from extremal finite sets, and analyzes the role of dangling points in surface-area minimization.
motivation: The research aims to understand whether dangling points in generating sets can affect the minimal surface area of Meissner polyhedra, potentially simplifying the search for area-minimizing bodies.
method: The author proves that removing a dangling point does not increase the smallest achievable surface area, and adding one cannot decrease it, using mathematical analysis of extremal sets.
result: The result reduces the search for area-minimizing Meissner polyhedra to generating sets without dangling points.
conclusion: The paper contributes to the geometric theory of constant-width bodies, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Optimal Sobolev Approximation By Deterministic And Random Shallow Sigmoidal Networks
authors: Yangshuai Wang Zhaohui Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shallow networks with prescribed or randomly sampled hidden parameters are widely used as numerical trial spaces, yet their optimal Sobolev approximation power with standard smooth sigmoidal activations in general dimension remains unresolved. We establish the corresponding optimal rates for a class of smooth sigmoidal activations with Schwartz-class derivative decay, including [MATH], the logistic sigmoid, and the error function [MATH]. We first construct deterministic direction--offset dictionaries with [MATH] features such that every [MATH] can be approximated with error of order [MATH] in [MATH] for all [MATH]. This rate is optimal in the sense of Kolmogorov widths for Sobolev balls. We further prove that dictionaries obtained by independent parameter sampling from any prescribed density bounded away from zero attain the same approximation exponent with high probability, up to logarithmic oversampling. The analysis develops a sigmoidal ridge representation and combines it with deterministic or probabilistic quadrature in direction--offset space while retaining polynomial control of the output coefficients. Numerical experiments across a broad range of dimensions, target regularities, and Sobolev error norms recover the predicted algebraic rates for both deterministic and random feature dictionaries.
tldr: This paper establishes optimal Sobolev approximation rates for shallow sigmoidal networks, covering both deterministic and random feature dictionaries.
motivation: Shallow networks with prescribed or random hidden parameters are widely used as trial spaces, but their optimal approximation power in Sobolev spaces was unresolved.
method: The authors introduce a sigmoidal ridge representation and combine it with deterministic or probabilistic quadrature in direction-offset space, while controlling output coefficients polynomially.
result: They prove optimal rates for deterministic dictionaries and show that random sampling from any bounded-away-from-zero density achieves the same exponent with high probability, up to logarithmic oversampling.
conclusion: This provides a complete characterization of approximation power for such networks, confirmed by numerical experiments across various dimensions and regularities.

title: Trustworthy Decisions In Reliability Set Estimation Under Insufficient Model Information
authors: Holger Dette, Zhengfu Liu, Jun Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliability set estimation identifies input regions where a response probability exceeds a target level, bridging estimation and safety-critical decisions. Practitioners typically start with a working model, an imperfect approximation of the true response surface. Relying on this imperfect model may incur decision risk, potentially certifying unsafe regions as safe. We develop a unified framework that turns such a working model into a trustworthy decision rule. First, a modeling-then-calibration procedure decouples estimation from decision. Since the true set is unobservable, we introduce an asymmetric, observable surrogate loss and use a separate calibration set to select a bias-correcting threshold, reducing decision risk and achieving [MATH] volume convergence. Second, we leverage conformal risk control with the surrogate loss to control false inclusion risk, which is the most safety-critical error, at a pre-specified level regardless of working model quality. Together, these calibration procedures show that a separate calibration set is necessary for risk control. Third, an adaptive design concentrates observations on the reliability set and its boundary, improving model quality where errors most affect decisions while controlling budget elsewhere. Numerical studies show not only more accurate set estimates but also calibrated finite-sample risk control that classical plug-in methods lack.
tldr: This paper develops a calibration and conformal risk control framework for reliability set estimation that ensures trustworthy decisions despite imperfect models.
motivation: Practitioners often use imperfect working models for reliability set estimation, which can lead to certification of unsafe regions as safe, creating decision risk.
method: The authors propose a modeling-then-calibration procedure using an asymmetric surrogate loss and a calibration set to select a bias-correcting threshold, and apply conformal risk control to control false inclusion risk. They also introduce an adaptive design to concentrate observations on the reliability set boundary.
result: The method achieves volume convergence and calibrated finite-sample risk control, outperforming classical plug-in methods in numerical studies.
conclusion: The framework ensures safety-critical decision risk is controlled even with insufficient model information, and a separate calibration set is necessary for risk control.

title: Sharp Dimension Bounds For Spline Spaces Over T-meshes With Highest Order Of Smoothness
authors: Falai Chen Bingru Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dimension of a polynomial spline space of bi-degree [MATH] over a T-mesh [MATH] with the highest order of smoothness [MATH] depends on both mesh topology and geometric configurations. Under the assumption that the T-connected components of the T-mesh [MATH] contain no vanishable T [MATH]-edges, we develop explicit upper and lower bounds of the dimension of the polynomial spline space. By introducing a decoupling technique within the completely non-diagonalizable component (CNDC) of the T-mesh [MATH], we separate tightly coupled multi-vertex constraints and transform global conformality conditions into localized linear equations along each interior large edge. Based on the decoupling technique, a new dimension formula of the polynomial spline space is then presented, and from which sharp upper and lower bounds of the dimension are obtained. The bounds are sharp in the sense that different geometric realizations of T-meshes with the same topology can attain the lower and upper bounds for the dimension of the polynomial spline space. We further prove that the new formula is consistent with Mourrain's homological dimension formula, and a sharper lower bound is obtained by our method.
tldr: This paper establishes sharp dimension bounds for polynomial spline spaces over T-meshes with highest order of smoothness using a decoupling technique.
motivation: The dimension of polynomial spline spaces over T-meshes depends on both topology and geometry, and the goal is to determine sharp bounds under specific conditions.
method: Introduces a decoupling technique within completely non-diagonalizable components (CNDC) to separate coupled constraints and localize conformality conditions along interior edges, leading to a new dimension formula.
result: Explicit upper and lower bounds are derived, with sharpness shown by geometric realizations achieving the bounds. The formula is consistent with Mourrain's homological dimension formula and yields a sharper lower bound.
conclusion: The work provides a novel dimension formula and sharp bounds, advancing the theory of spline spaces over T-meshes.

title: To Control Or Not To Control
authors: Odysseas Kanavetas, Camiel M. P. Koopmans, Floske M. Spieksma
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a model with control vacations instead of standard queueing control systems with permanent control. The researched model is an M/M/1 queue with temporary periods of service rate control with two available service rates. After a control period of exponentially distributed length, a control vacation is initiated during which a fixed service rate [MATH] is used. The start of the next control period needs to be scheduled directly at a certain cost. We will use the Markov Decision Process from Kanavetas et al. arXiv:2605.31573 to find a sufficient condition that ensures that the average expected cost can be reduced w.r.t. the model that only uses the fixed service rate. Under this condition we will use properties of this related process to construct a cost reducing policy. The process with control vacations under specific policies induces a renewal reward process. We use a Tauberian theorem to relate the average expected cost of this renewal reward process to a vanishing discount method and analytically determine a lower bound of the average expected cost reduction. Finally, we study the actual attained average cost reduction for these policies through simulation.
tldr: This paper studies an M/M/1 queue with control vacations, using a Markov Decision Process to find a condition under which average expected cost can be reduced, and constructs a cost-reducing policy with a simulation study.
motivation: Standard queueing control systems assume permanent control, but in practice, control may be temporary, so this paper introduces control vacations.
method: Uses a Markov Decision Process model from a prior paper, derives a sufficient condition for cost reduction, constructs a policy, and analyzes the resulting renewal reward process using a Tauberian theorem for the average cost, then simulates.
result: Provides a sufficient condition for cost reduction and analytically determines a lower bound on the average expected cost reduction, with simulation results showing actual attained reductions.
conclusion: Control vacations can be beneficial in reducing average expected cost under certain conditions, and the proposed policy yields cost reductions.

title: Combining Concurrent And Historical Functional Linear Regression
authors: Alois Kneip, Dominik Liebl, Sven Otto
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a function-on-function linear regression model in which the response at time [MATH] depends on both the past trajectory of a predictor and its concurrent value. The model combines an [MATH]-historical effect with a point-evaluation effect, and these two coefficient functions are not automatically identifiable. We characterize the resulting non-identifiability and show that the concurrent and historical effects are separately identifiable whenever the covariance eigenfunctions of the covariance operator of the predictor are not pointwise square-summable. This mild and novel condition prevents the concurrent point evaluation from being represented by an [MATH]-historical effect. Building on an orthogonalized representation of the predictor process, we propose a smoothing-spline estimator for both coefficient functions and establish consistency rates. The rates reveal an interesting trade-off between path regularity and eigenvalue decay: smoother predictor trajectories lead to faster convergence of the historical-effect estimator, whereas rougher trajectories lead to faster convergence of the concurrent-effect estimator. Simulation studies and two real-data applications demonstrate the practical importance of disentangling concurrent and historical effects.
tldr: This paper proposes a functional linear regression model that combines concurrent and historical effects, addressing identifiability and estimation.
motivation: To separately identify and estimate concurrent and historical effects in function-on-function regression, which are not automatically identifiable.
method: Uses an orthogonalized representation of the predictor process and a smoothing-spline estimator for both coefficient functions.
result: Characterizes non-identifiability, proves separate identifiability under a mild condition, and establishes consistency rates with a trade-off between path regularity and eigenvalue decay.
conclusion: Simulations and real-data applications show the practical importance of disentangling concurrent and historical effects.

title: Efficient Flatness-based Computation Of Trajectories For Vehicles With Many Trailers
authors: Basile Graf, Gustave Lapierre, Philippe M\"ullhaupt
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address the practical computation of feedforward steering inputs for a car with n trailers via differential flatness. The standard route (iterated symbolic differentiation of the flat output) scales prohibitively with n: even with computer-algebra software the expression sizes grow super-exponentially and become intractable beyond n approx. 5. We propose an algorithm that combines four ingredients (angular intermediate variables, factorisation of the recursion in submaps, rescaled higher-order product/quotient rules, and a composition rule based on truncated formal power series instead of Faa di Bruno's formula). We benchmark the proposed method against (i) direct symbolic differentiation in SymPy and (ii) Faa di Bruno's formula evaluated via Bell polynomials. Both reference methods hit a clear computational wall: SymPy reaches a 20 s timeout at derivative order r = 14, while the Bell-polynomial recursion exceeds a 60 s timeout beyond r = 24. The proposed approach has O(r3) arithmetic complexity in the derivative order and remains under one millisecond up to r = 40, with numerical agreement to machine precision in the regime where the reference methods succeed. As an end-to-end illustration, a 20-trailer parking manoeuvre is computed and animated.
tldr: 提出一种基于微分平坦性的高效轨迹计算方法，用于带有多个拖车的车辆，克服了符号微分在拖车数量增加时的计算爆炸问题。
motivation: 标准符号微分方法在拖车数量多时计算规模呈超指数增长，难以处理超过约5个拖车的情况。
method: 结合角度中间变量、递归分解、重缩放高阶导数规则以及基于截断形式幂级数的组合规则，实现了O(r^3)复杂度的轨迹计算。
result: 与SymPy和Bell多项式方法相比，新方法在40阶导数下保持毫秒级计算时间，且数值精度达到机器精度。
conclusion: 该方法可高效计算带20个拖车的停车轨迹，为多拖车车辆控制提供实用工具。

title: The Symmetry And Linear Stability Of Convex 1+5 Coorbital Central Configurations With Homogeneous Potential
authors: Jiangtao Xu Yiyang Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.19958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the planar Newtonian 1+N-body problem when the N masses tend to zero, the corresponding relative equilibria become coorbital around the dominant mass. In this work, we focus on convex central configurations in the planar 1+N coorbital problem. For the 1+5 coorbital problem with the homogeneous potential, we prove that any convex coorbital central configuration with symmetric masses must have an axis of symmetry. Furthermore, under explicit restrictions on the angular variables in a homogeneous potential, we prove the linear stability of both convex symmetric 1+5 and convex 1+N coorbital central configurations.
tldr: This paper proves symmetry and linear stability properties of convex central configurations in the planar 1+5 coorbital problem with homogeneous potential.
motivation: To understand the structure and stability of coorbital configurations in celestial mechanics, which are relevant for planetary systems.
method: The authors analyze the 1+N coorbital problem with homogeneous potential, focusing on convex configurations, and use symmetry arguments and linear stability analysis.
result: They prove that any convex coorbital central configuration with symmetric masses has an axis of symmetry for the 1+5 case, and establish linear stability under specific angular restrictions for both 1+5 and general 1+N symmetric configurations.
conclusion: The results extend knowledge of central configurations in the coorbital problem, providing rigorous symmetry and stability criteria.

title: Sets Of Nice Recurrence Are Partition Regular
authors: Jonathan Chapman
abstract: ArXiv:2608.20004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A set of positive integers [MATH] is called a set of nice recurrence if for any measure preserving system [MATH], for all measurable [MATH], and each [MATH], there exists [MATH] such that [MATH].
